generic_components.name: Observation loading and voxel downsampling
generic_components.what: prim_potlid.load_obs l.81-86 and prim_boards.load_obs l.67-74: load pts, cam (and frame), then 1.5 mm voxel dedupe. Unchanged for any object.
reusable_for: all 11 objects (spoon only if obs points exist)

generic_components.name: manifold3d mesh plumbing and union
generic_components.what: to_mf/from_mf l.93-104, frame_T l.107, mf_cylinder/mf_sphere l.112-121, union l.609-611 (prim_potlid); to_trimesh l.414-416 (prim_boards). Batch-boolean union into one watertight mesh.

generic_components.name: Residual clustering
generic_components.what: prim_potlid.clusters l.186-199: 3 mm voxel occupancy, 1-voxel dilation, 26-connectivity labels, largest first. Shape-agnostic.
reusable_for: all objects with appendages or markers: cups, pot, lid, pitcher, rack, sweeper, dust pan, boards

generic_components.name: Marker-ball detector and sphere fit (two implementations)
generic_components.what: prim_potlid.fit_sphere l.203-235 + markers_from l.238-291 (free radius 5-9.5 mm or 7 mm prior, gap test against any body mesh, stem only with point support against a 20 mm-offset control); prim_boards.fit_sphere l.173-182 + find_markers l.185-252 (centre votes p - R0 n, mean shift, soft-L1 LSQ with a radius prior, >= 10 frames). Both are object-agnostic given a body surface. They duplicate each other with different thresholds; prim_rack reuses the prim_potlid version [M code].
reusable_for: all 11 objects: every scan carries the same mocap balls on stems (README sec. 1, [D])

generic_components.name: Open-container lathe axis search
generic_components.what: fib_hemisphere l.295-300 + pot_axis l.303-355: 600 hemisphere directions, axis line placed by line-complex LSQ (lathe_obs._place), score = rim flatness MAD + rotational self-consistency, then local refinement around the 3 best. Generic for open containers of revolution, not tied to the pot's size.
reusable_for: water_pitcher body (only if it is close to a surface of revolution: rot-consistency 8.85 mm on ep22 [M])

generic_components.name: Thin-wall lathe profile with a closed floor
generic_components.what: pot_body l.358-450 with binned_sector_median l.124-142, fill_smooth, curve_normals, resample, poly_dist, revolve_to_object: polar profile about an interior point; outer and inner points split by view direction; wall t from both curves; median over >= 6 of 24 sectors drops handles and markers; closed floor = inner floor offset by t; rim cap at the robust rim height.

generic_components.name: Lathe residual mask and TSDF-appendage hybrid
generic_components.what: residual_mask l.453-458 (points outside the revolved hull by > APP_D) and tsdf_parts l.597-606 (body + our own library TSDF faces lying outside it). The tsdf variant is a fully generic appendage treatment: no handle model at all.
reusable_for: any lathe object with appendages: cups (handles), pot, pitcher (handle, spout)

generic_components.name: Shallow surface-of-revolution centring and tilt refinement
generic_components.what: Inside build_lid: circle fit to the per-sector outer edge l.636-649 and the tilt least squares h_ij = h0_i + r_i (gx cos th + gy sin th) l.660-684 (about 40 lines). Generic for any disc-like body of revolution; the surrounding lid code is not.
reusable_for: the pot's floor or rim plane in principle
a dish or plate if one existed

generic_components.name: Swept rectangle along a planar curve
generic_components.what: The sweep loop in arch_strap l.788-806: rectangle (W x T) swept along a resampled 2-D curve, capped and converted to a manifold. A generalized-cylinder primitive with a fixed cross-section.
reusable_for: cup and pitcher loop handles (needs a centreline fit in the handle plane)

generic_components.name: Planar slab: plane, two-face thickness, in-plane frame
generic_components.what: prim_boards.wmode l.77-86, fit_plane l.90-121 (normal = principal direction of PCA normals, view-weighted face modes, joint two-face refit), inplane_frame l.124-133, and the thickness logic in fit l.455-470 (two faces if both have >= NFACE points, else a family default).

generic_components.name: 2-D occupancy outline to polygon
generic_components.what: occupancy l.256-261, disk, _close, clean_mask l.273-287 (closing, hole fill, opening, component bridging), mask_polygon l.290-304 (Gaussian-smoothed contour, approxPolyDP), rect_polygon l.403-410 (min-area rectangle). Any planar part seen from its face.

the pot handle (a direct replacement for bar_handle's hand-built bar+tip+hole)

generic_components.name: Extrusion + spheres + stems mesh builder
generic_components.what: prim_boards.build_mesh l.419-444: CrossSection polygon extruded between the face planes, optional cut-out, marker spheres and stems unioned, mapped back to the object frame.

generic_components.name: Family driver and GT-free selector
generic_components.what: prim_boards.build l.567-589 (variant loop) and run l.592-649: pass 1 family parameter (median two-face thickness), pass 2 all (episode x variant) candidates, selection = lowest obs_fidelity sum_mm over all of the object's episodes. Nothing in run() depends on boards except the default arguments.
reusable_for: all 11 objects; it is the natural core of an automatic template router

generic_components.name: Debug overlay
generic_components.what: prim_boards.save_debug l.546-564: occupancy image with outline, slot and markers.

object_specific_rules.name: Template choice per object (part list)
object_specific_rules.object: white_pot, white_pot_lid, wooden_piece_1/2 (and the rack in prim_rack.py)
object_specific_rules.rule: The CLI hard-wires the template: prim_potlid main l.816 accepts only {pot, lid}; build_pot l.559-594 = lathe body + one flat bar handle + markers; build_lid l.628-746 = domed sheet + one arch strap + markers; prim_boards = slab - slot + markers, defaults objects wooden_piece_1,wooden_piece_2 and episodes 23,24 (l.662). A person (agent) assigns object to script; nothing refuses a wrong object.
object_specific_rules.why_needed: The agents wrote one fitter per object type after looking at that object's points and crops; the part list is the object knowledge.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Run every family fitter (container lathe, sheet of revolution, slab/extrusion, swept tube, TSDF fallback) on every object, gate with each fitter's own diagnostics (rot-consistency, bins_both, residual share, two-face counts), select by obs_fidelity with a complexity penalty, and keep library_v3 as a candidate. The object name or a VLM looking at the colour crops may propose a family; names are an allowed input (lit/primitives-cad.md sec. 5.4 case c). [M] in this audit obs_fidelity ranked library_v3 above every wrong-template fit on the dust pan and the pitcher. [H] the router picks the hand-chosen template on pot, lid, rack and cups; falsified if it picks another template on any of them.

object_specific_rules.name: Handle = residual cluster reaching > 60 mm beyond the body
object_specific_rules.rule: build_pot l.571-578: among residual clusters with >= 200 points, the first whose P99 distance from the axis exceeds rmax + 60 mm is the handle.
object_specific_rules.why_needed: Separates the pot's long pan handle from marker clusters (stems <= 20 mm) and noise bands. The number is set by the pot's handle length (~172 mm fitted, [M] ep41/42 JSON).
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Classify every residual cluster by fitting all generic part models (sphere, extruded outline in the cluster's PCA plane, swept tube, TSDF patch) and choose per cluster by fidelity + description length; no reach threshold. Or make the threshold relative to the marker gap (MK_GAP 20 mm) rather than an absolute 60 mm.

object_specific_rules.name: Handle is a straight flat bar with a rounded tip and one hole near the tip
object_specific_rules.rule: bar_handle l.461-550: plane by trimmed fit to top-seen points, width = median P3-P97 per 5 mm bin, thickness = 2 x median depth of side-seen points clipped to 3-8 mm (else BAR_T0 5 mm), inner end inside the wall, semicircular tip, hole = closed gap >= 40 mm2 within 60 mm of the tip and within half the half-width of the centre line; in_bar l.553-556 removes bar points before the marker search.
object_specific_rules.why_needed: The pot's pan handle is a flat bar with a hanging hole. The hole was never found in our occupancy (README sec. 9, [D] defects list).
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Replace with the boards' generic outline code: project the cluster onto its own fitted plane, occupancy -> clean_mask -> mask_polygon -> extrude between two fitted face planes (prim_boards l.256-304, 419-444). Seen holes then come out of the occupancy for free. [H] pot CD-O stays within +-0.01 cm of 0.342 [D]; falsified in a pre-registered scan round.

object_specific_rules.name: Open end = the end with fewer near-axis points
object_specific_rules.rule: pot_axis l.325-327 and pot_body l.366-375: count points with r < 0.4 R in the bottom vs top 25 % of height; the end with more is the floor.
object_specific_rules.why_needed: Containers have surface near the axis only at the floor. It fails for lids and plates (no open end), so the lid needed a separate code path (up = towards the cameras, l.632-634).
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Fit both orientations and keep the one with the lower fidelity, or use the camera-side rule (the table side is never seen), which is generic for any object resting on a table.

object_specific_rules.name: Polar profile origin at 60 % of the height
object_specific_rules.rule: pot_body l.379: hO = hlo + 0.6 (hhi - hlo); the profile is parameterised by polar angle about (0, hO).
object_specific_rules.why_needed: Lets one polar curve follow wall, rounded bottom corner and floor of a deep pot. It assumes the profile is star-shaped from that point.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Use an arclength-parameterised profile (e.g. principal curve or ordered medial curve in the (r, h) half-plane) instead of a polar one; or choose hO by fidelity over a small grid.

object_specific_rules.name: Lid: disc axis = smallest PCA direction, up = towards the cameras
object_specific_rules.rule: build_lid l.631-634, then a circle fit to the outer edge in 36 sectors l.636-649.
object_specific_rules.why_needed: The lid is only seen from above; it has no open end for the container rule.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: A flatness test on the PCA eigenvalue ratio routes an object to the sheet-of-revolution fitter instead of the container fitter. Both rules are generic once the family is chosen.

object_specific_rules.name: Lid flange window 40-80 mm
object_specific_rules.rule: build_lid l.652-659: re-fit the disc normal on points with 40 < r < 80 mm and |h - median| < 6 mm.
object_specific_rules.why_needed: The lid's flat flange annulus gives a clean plane for the axis; the window is this lid's absolute dimensions (r_edge ~95 mm).
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Make the window relative (e.g. 0.45-0.85 r_edge), or drop it and rely on the generic tilt refinement at l.660-684.

object_specific_rules.name: Dome fill under the arch, r = 15-35 mm
object_specific_rules.rule: lid_top_profile l.615-625: inside r < 15 mm the top height is a quadratic in r^2 fitted on 15-35 mm.
object_specific_rules.why_needed: The strap handle hides the lid top near the axis.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Define the window from the occluded region (radial bins with < MINSEC sectors, or the arch cluster's footprint), or fill with fill_smooth like the pot profile.

object_specific_rules.name: Lid sheet thickness prior 2.5 mm
object_specific_rules.rule: T_LID l.75 (env PRIM_T_LID); underside = top - t.
object_specific_rules.why_needed: The underside is never seen, so thickness cannot be measured from our points. The first 2.5 mm came from a brief that quoted scan walls (leak, work log 2026-10-27); the clean-up round passed at 1.5/2.5/4.0 mm [D].
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Not from our points. Keep a class prior with the 'pass at every grid value' rule; obs_fidelity cannot choose it (biased toward thinner sheets).

object_specific_rules.name: Arch = first residual cluster with > 50 mm in-plane extent; swept strap model
object_specific_rules.rule: build_lid l.728-735 picks the cluster (>= 100 points); arch_strap l.749-810 sweeps a rectangle (width clipped 8-30 mm, T clipped 3-8 mm or BAR_T0) along the P75 top-height curve; ends run down to the sheet mid-surface.
object_specific_rules.why_needed: The lid's handle is a strap arch over the top.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: The same per-cluster model selection as the pot handle: a generic swept-tube fitter (centreline from an L1-medial skeleton or a PCA-plane spline, fitted cross-section) vs extrusion vs TSDF patch, chosen by fidelity.

object_specific_rules.name: Crossing board: the other board through the slot
object_specific_rules.rule: crossing_board l.137-169 (RANSAC line on in-plane-normal points > 4 mm beyond the slab, tol 6 mm, >= 300 inliers, >= 30 mm extent); fit l.471-487 drops its strip from the outline and excludes tb/2 + 4 mm from markers.
object_specific_rules.why_needed: In assembled frames the other board's points are inside our track's crop and would corrupt outline and markers.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Generic foreign-surface removal: drop points that are not rigid with the track over frames, or subtract the other tracked object's own mesh at its own tracked pose (both GT-free). [M] on the dust pan this rule fired on the pan's own walls (1,350 inliers, 59 deg) and dropped 951 of its points.

object_specific_rules.name: Slot = line of hits from one long edge to mid-width, perpendicular, one side only
object_specific_rules.rule: slot_from_grid l.337-400: hit-grid contrast of a 7 mm band vs 12 mm flanks >= 0.35 with the other half <= 0.15, >= 20 mm from the ends, within 10 mm of a crossing line at <= 15 deg (l.507), width 4-20 mm (W_MIN/W_MAX l.61); slot_from_crossing l.307-334 (side by 1.5x density) is recorded only as a diagnostic.
object_specific_rules.why_needed: The boards join by halving slots. [M] candidates.jsonl: the slot was carved in all 8 board-2 candidates and in none of the 8 board-1 candidates; board 2 then failed for a different reason (wrong board's track, ADD 78.7 mm [D]).
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Hard to automate from one object's points alone. Generic version: carve any slab region that another tracked object's mesh occupies in assembled frames (an interpenetration constraint, not object knowledge). It needs identity-safe tracks first (README sec. 9).

object_specific_rules.name: Board thickness window and default
object_specific_rules.rule: fit l.457-461: two-face thickness accepted only if 3-25 mm, else the family default (median two-face t over the family's episodes, run l.601-606; fallback 8 mm).
object_specific_rules.why_needed: One face is often unseen; the family default shares evidence across episodes and boards.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Already semi-automatic (family pass). The 3 mm floor and the 8 mm fallback are board priors: [M] the 2.7 mm dust pan sheet [D wall] became an 8 mm plate.

object_specific_rules.name: Variant sets per family
object_specific_rules.object: pot/lid (fit, nostem, tsdf, thick); boards (occ, occ_d2, rect, occ_nm)
object_specific_rules.rule: Hand-chosen variant lists (prim_potlid l.817, prim_boards l.657/663); the GT-free selector picks among them.
object_specific_rules.why_needed: Pre-registered at most 4 variants per family.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: This is already the automated part: generate candidates, select by fidelity. Extending the variant set to the other families' templates gives the router of rule 1.

hand_constants.name: VOX / VOX_DS / GRID
hand_constants.note: prim_potlid l.56, prim_boards l.51-52. Stereo resolution; same for all objects.

hand_constants.name: NSEC / MINSEC / MIN_PTS / DPHI
hand_constants.note: prim_potlid l.57-60. Lathe sector statistics. MINSEC 6 of 24 assumes an appendage covers < 90 deg of azimuth.

hand_constants.name: APP_D
hand_constants.note: prim_potlid l.61 (also prim_rack l.74). Residual threshold set by stereo noise 5-10 mm. Side effect: any real feature less than 8 mm proud (rim lip, spout lip, ribs) is absorbed or dropped.

hand_constants.name: CL_VOX
hand_constants.note: prim_potlid l.62, clustering voxel.

hand_constants.name: Marker set A (prim_potlid)
hand_constants.value: MK_MIN 60 pts; MK_DIAG 6-35 mm; MK_RES 2 mm; MK_GAP -3..+20 mm; MK_R0 7 mm; radius 5-9.5 mm; STEM_MIN 15; STEM_R 3.5 mm; free-fit accept median res < 1.2 mm and spread > 0.08; re-cluster above APP_D + 4 mm; stem if gap > 3 mm, control offset 20 mm, n_stem >= 2 n_ctl
hand_constants.note: l.63-70, 224, 257, 275-287. The same balls on every object; R0 from our own spoon stereo. [M] on the dust pan a flat patch passed as a ball with a stem (prior fit at 1.8 mm residual < MK_RES).

hand_constants.name: Marker set B (prim_boards)
hand_constants.value: R0 7 mm, SIG_R 1.5 mm; MIN_MPTS 25; MIN_MFRAMES 10; extent <= 30 mm; 16 mm neighbourhood; 3 mm mean-shift; 2.5 mm inliers; r 4-11 mm; RMS <= 1.6 mm; centre <= half + 16 mm; dedupe 8 mm; attached <= r + 2 mm; stem radial < 4 mm, stem_r 1.5-4 mm
hand_constants.note: l.57-60, 195-249. The same physical balls with a different detector and thresholds from set A.

hand_constants.name: NSEG
hand_constants.note: prim_potlid l.77, revolve segments.

hand_constants.name: T_MIN / T_MAX and the fallback wall
hand_constants.value: 2-6 mm; 4 mm if fewer than 3 profile bins see both walls
hand_constants.note: prim_potlid l.71, 405-407. Family prior for thin moulded walls. It would clamp the sweeper's 13 mm [D wall]. [M] the pitcher run had 1 bin with both walls and fell back to 4 mm.

hand_constants.name: T_LID
hand_constants.note: prim_potlid l.75. Lid underside never seen; first value leaked from scan measurements; clean-up passed at all three [D].

hand_constants.name: BAR_T0
hand_constants.note: prim_potlid l.76; handle/strap thickness when no side-seen points.

hand_constants.name: pot_axis search
hand_constants.value: 600 directions; rim window [0.6 R, R + 20 mm]; open-end test r < 0.4 R in the end 25 % of height; >= 12 of 24 sectors; local grids +-6 deg step 2 deg, then +-2 deg step 0.7 deg
hand_constants.note: l.303-353. Open-container family; meaningless for lids and plates.

hand_constants.name: pot_body geometry thresholds
hand_constants.value: body r < P60(r) + 20 mm; polar origin at 60 % of height; view split |s| > 0.3; rim points within 8 mm of the mid curve, r > 0.5 rmax, > 30 per sector, P99; resample 3 mm
hand_constants.note: l.367, 379, 383, 417-434. Container family. The 20 mm and 8 mm are absolute, sized for 10-20 cm containers.

hand_constants.name: Handle detector
hand_constants.value: >= 200 points and P99 radius > rmax + 60 mm
hand_constants.note: build_pot l.571, 577. Pot's long handle.

hand_constants.name: bar_handle parameters
hand_constants.value: 5 mm bins >= 15 pts; width P3-P97; top view > 0.3, side view > 0.5; T clipped to 3-8 mm; tip P99.5; inner search from 60 mm before; hole grid 2 mm, area >= 40 mm2, within 60 mm of the tip, |a| < half/2

hand_constants.name: Lid edge and tilt
hand_constants.value: 36 edge sectors, P98, 3 mm band, > 50 pts; tilt bins 2 mm / 4 mm, surface +-4 mm, r > 20 mm, 3 iterations
hand_constants.note: l.639-683. Usable for any disc-like body of revolution; the r > 20 mm is absolute.

hand_constants.name: Lid flange window
hand_constants.note: l.652-654. Absolute dimensions of this lid.

hand_constants.name: Lid dome window
hand_constants.note: lid_top_profile l.615. The region under the arch.

hand_constants.name: Lid residual and arch detector
hand_constants.value: h > top + APP_D and r < r_edge + 15 mm; arch = first cluster >= 100 pts with in-plane extent > 50 mm

hand_constants.name: arch_strap parameters
hand_constants.value: 3 mm bins, >= 8 top-seen pts, P75 height; width clipped to 8-30 mm; T clipped to 3-8 mm; end extension 4 mm; resample 2 mm

hand_constants.name: COS_FACE and plane refit
hand_constants.value: 0.9; refine |n.a| > 0.85; >= 200 face points; +-2 mm; accept refit within 10 deg
hand_constants.note: prim_boards l.53, 95, 109-118. Any planar slab.

hand_constants.name: NFACE
hand_constants.note: prim_boards l.54. An absolute count, so it depends on plate area and episode length; small plates fall back to the default thickness.

hand_constants.name: SLAB_M / MOFF
hand_constants.note: prim_boards l.55-56. Face jitter is about +-2 mm.

hand_constants.name: Slab thickness window and default
hand_constants.value: accept 3-25 mm; else family median; fallback 8 mm
hand_constants.note: prim_boards l.457-461, 606. Board prior. [M] it gave the 2.7 mm dust pan sheet 8 mm.

hand_constants.name: Outline cleaning
hand_constants.value: closing 3 mm; opening 3 cells (4.5 mm); components >= 10 % of the largest; closing grows to <= 14 cells (21 mm); smoothing 1.5 cells; EPS 1 mm
hand_constants.note: prim_boards l.62-63, 273, 448.

hand_constants.name: rect body opening
hand_constants.note: prim_boards l.499. Drops anything narrower than ~16 mm (tabs, but also real handles).

hand_constants.name: Crossing-board RANSAC
hand_constants.value: |cn| < 0.35 and > 4 mm beyond the slab; 400 iters, tol 6 mm, >= 300 inliers, >= 30 mm extent; strip tb/2 + 1.5 mm dropped, tb/2 + 4 mm excluded

hand_constants.name: Slot detector
hand_constants.value: crossing <= 15 deg; width 4-20 mm; 1 mm grid; 6 mm interior erosion; 7 mm band vs 12 mm flanks at 15 mm; contrast >= 0.35 with the other half <= 0.15; >= 20 mm from the ends; within 10 mm of the crossing; hits >= 2; depth clipped to +-0.2 W; cut 0.2 m long; side ratio 1.5

hand_constants.name: One-board check
hand_constants.note: prim_boards l.522-523, diagnostic only.

Docstring + CLI: 62 (8 %). prim_boards.py (628): generic: 293 (47 %): imports 10, constants 12, load/wmode 18, markers 77, outline 41, rect 8, build_mesh 27, save_debug 19, build 23, run driver + fidelity selection 58. Planar-slab family: 111 (18 %): fit_plane + inplane_frame 42, fit() without the crossing and slot blocks 69. Generic code is also duplicated: two marker detectors (88 vs 77 lines) with different thresholds for the same balls. prim_rack.py (884 lines, not counted) reuses prim_potlid.markers_from and lathe_obs.normals; by function names its tray, cup and peg fitters are rack-specific.
new_object_failure_modes: No router or refusal: prim_potlid main l.816 accepts only {pot, lid} and stamps object='white_pot'/'white_pot_lid' into the JSON (l.560, 629) whatever the input; prim_boards defaults to the boards (l.662). [M] All four wrong-object runs below exited 0 and wrote watertight meshes. A wrong template looks like success; only the selector catches it.

Water pitcher via 'prim_potlid.py pot obs/ep22_water_pitcher.npz' (250,235 points after voxels, 2 min 19 s wall) [M]: axis rot-consistency 8.85 mm vs 2.1-2.3 mm on the pot (ep41/ep42 JSONs); axis J 12.3 mm vs 3.0; fit_axis 12.3 deg away. Only 1 profile bin saw both walls (pot: 20-24), so the wall fell back to the 4 mm default. The 'handle' cluster had 81,681 points, 33 % of all points (pot: 13.6-20.2 k, 5-7 %). It was built as a straight flat bar 123 x 37.8 x 8 mm (8 mm = the clip ceiling) tilted 49.7 deg; no hole. The output has 2 disconnected bodies and 0 accepted markers. GT-free fidelity sum 24.1 mm vs 7.05 mm for library_v3. [H] mechanism: the spout and the loop handle are not radial bars, and the weak axis puts body surface into the residual. Falsify: re-run with the tsdf variant (generic appendages) and check whether fidelity approaches library_v3.

Mini dust pan via 'prim_boards.py build obs/ep39_mini_dust_pan.npz' (25 s) [M]: thickness = default 8 mm. The ~2.7 mm sheet [D wall] is below the 3 mm acceptance floor and its underside is unseen. A 'crossing board' was detected on the pan's own walls or handle (1,350 inliers, 59 deg) and 951 points were dropped from the outline. Slot undecided, 0 markers. Output: a flat 183 x 168 mm plate 8 mm thick (occ 136 faces, rect 12 faces); walls and handle gone. Fidelity 4.83 mm (occ) and 9.82 mm (rect) vs 3.64 mm for library_v3.

Mini dust pan via 'prim_potlid.py pot' (1 min 56 s) [M]: the lathe does not refuse it. Rot-consistency 2.71 mm is close to the pot's 2.1-2.3 mm, the same false pass approach2 found with its lathe gate. Body radius 58.8 mm for a pan about 17 cm across [D extents]; only 6 outer profile bins; residual 31 % of points; no handle (nothing reached 60 mm). One 'marker ball' with a stem was accepted on a flat patch (free radius 4.9 m, then the 7 mm prior at 1.8 mm median residual, under MK_RES 2 mm). Fidelity 5.79 mm.

Mini dust pan via 'prim_potlid.py lid' (24 s) [M]: also runs silently. Result: a flat (dome 0 mm) 2.5 mm sheet of radius 97 mm plus a 150 mm 'arch strap' (12.2 mm wide, 20 mm high) swept over whichever residual cluster exceeded 50 mm. Residual share 11.3 %, same as the real lid's 11.9 %, so the internal diagnostics do not flag it. Fidelity 4.93 mm.

Safety net that worked [M]: obs_fidelity put library_v3 first on both new objects (dust pan 3.64 < 4.83 < 4.93 < 5.79 < 9.82 mm; pitcher 7.05 < 24.1 mm). Caveats [D]: its Spearman 0.85 vs CD-O was measured on pot candidates only, and it prefers thinner sheets where the underside is unseen. [H] On an object with an unseen underside it could prefer a wrong thin template over the TSDF. Falsify in a pre-registered scan round by running every template on every public object.

Absolute-size windows break at other scales: handle reach 60 mm (l.577), lid flange 40-80 mm (l.652), dome 15-35 mm (l.615), arch > 50 mm (l.733), body r < P60 + 20 mm (l.367), rim window R + 20 mm (l.329), NFACE 1500 points (l.54), slot >= 20 mm from the ends (l.377), slab thickness 3-25 mm (l.457).

Part types with no fitter: loop handles (cups, pitcher), the spout (needs a displacement field, lit sec. 2.4), generalized cylinders (spoon, sweeper ring handle), the sweeper bristle block, folded sheets (dust pan). T_MAX 6 mm would clamp the sweeper's 13 mm walls [D wall, H effect].

Input format: prim_boards.slot_from_grid l.345 needs the 'hits', 'lo', 'vox' keys. [M] Every single-episode obs file has them; the merged obs/ep21+22_blue_cup.npz does not, so prim_boards on it would raise KeyError.
The marker code is duplicated with different thresholds (prim_potlid set A vs prim_boards set B), so the same physical balls are accepted or rejected differently per object family [M code].
audits.summary:
Honest answer to "are the meshes made case by case?": partly, yes. [M] Of the 1,397 non-blank lines in prim_potlid.py and prim_boards.py, about 38 % is generic plumbing that would run on any object: loading, clustering, marker balls, manifold union, 2-D outline extrusion, and the multi-episode driver with GT-free selection. About 19 % is reusable within a shape family: the open-container lathe (axis search, thin-wall profile, closed floor) and the planar slab. About 33 % encodes knowledge of one object, all of it chosen by an agent after looking at that object: the part list (pot = lathe + bar handle; lid = domed sheet + strap; boards = slab - slot), which residual cluster is the handle ('reaches > 60 mm beyond the body', l.577; 'in-plane extent > 50 mm', l.733), the flat-bar-with-hole model, the lid's 40-80 mm flange window and 15-35 mm dome window, the 2.5 mm lid thickness, and the board crossing/slot logic. Once a template is chosen, everything is automatic: every number is fitted to our points, variants are generated, and the GT-free fidelity picks the winner. The template choice itself is not automatic.

What happens on a new object [M, run here on our own points, $0, no scans]. Run on the pitcher, the dust pan and the dust pan again with the lid template, the fitters never refuse: all four runs produced watertight but wrong meshes.
- Pitcher as 'pot': axis error 8.85 mm vs 2.1-2.3 on the pot, and a third of the points became an 8 mm flat bar.
- Dust pan as a board: a flat 8 mm plate with walls and handle gone.
- Dust pan as a lid: a disc with a phantom strap.
The fidelity selector caught every one of them and kept library_v3 (dust pan 3.64 mm vs 4.8-9.8 mm; pitcher 7.05 vs 24.1 mm).

The automated route, from components that already exist here:
1. Turn the run() driver into a router: run every family fitter plus the TSDF fallback on every object, gate on each fitter's own diagnostics, and select by fidelity with a complexity penalty.
2. Replace the part-specific appendage code (bar_handle, arch_strap) with generic per-cluster models chosen by fidelity: sphere, extruded outline in the cluster's own plane (the boards' outline code), swept tube, or TSDF patch (the tsdf variant).
3. Make the absolute windows relative to the object's fitted size.
4. Let the object name, or a VLM on the colour crops, only propose a family; the fit and the selector decide.
5. Accept that thicknesses we never see (the lid and rack undersides) remain priors, tested with the rule 'pass at every grid value'.

[L] lit/primitives-cad.md sec. 4 finds no paper that runs the full 'VLM writes a template, optimiser fits it to real depth' loop near 1 % Chamfer. GeoCode and ShapeAssembly fit hand-written programs; Efficient RANSAC detects planes, spheres, cylinders, cones and tori. Two caveats on the selector [D]: fidelity was validated only on pot candidates (Spearman 0.85), and it prefers thin sheets where the underside is unseen. Approach2 found that the dust pan and spoon falsely pass the lathe gate, and the rot-consistency here (2.71 mm on the dust pan) shows the same.

[H] A fidelity router reproduces the hand template choice on pot, lid, rack and cups and keeps library_v3 where no template fits. Falsified if it picks a different template on any of those in a pre-registered scan round.

Integrity note: while listing observation-file keys, my first glob also matched *_align.npz. np.load opened one archive (obs/ep21+22_blue_cup_align.npz) and raised on the missing 'pts' key; no array or key list from it was read or printed. I re-ran with *_align.npz excluded. No repo files were edited, nothing was committed, no scans were read or scored.

generic_components.name: obs_points.py (whole file, main L28-145)
generic_components.what: Turns our stereo depth along our own track into object-frame surface points. It back-projects ROI pixels and drops flying pixels (edge filter L70), the table band (per-frame refit of the frame-0 RANSAC plane, L87-99), hand/forearm capsules (L100-105) and other tracked objects (L106-110). A free-space/hit vote on a 4 mm voxel grid then keeps only points rigidly attached to the object (L114-141). Nothing in it is object-specific: it needs only the object name (for cam_T_<obj>), a pose file, depth, hands and an ROI mesh (bounds only).
reusable_for: all 11 objects, wherever a correct track exists (it fails upstream on the beige-cup ep11 frame-0 track and the ep23 board-identity track, README s4)

generic_components.name: obs_fidelity.py (whole file, L8-24)
generic_components.what: GT-free selector. Trimmed (90 %) mean obs->mesh distance plus mesh->obs distance, the latter counted only inside the observations' axis-aligned bounding box. Object-agnostic. Limits: it has no ICP, so it only scores meshes already in our track frame, and the documented --icp/--trim flags are not implemented (passing --trim 0.5 crashes with 'string is not a file: 0.5' [M]). Known bias toward thin sheets where the underside is unseen.
reusable_for: also usable as a 'does this shape family apply' gate against the library_v3 baseline: rejected 6/6 wrong-family meshes in this audit [M]

generic_components.name: lathe_obs.py: fit_axis L114-154 (+ normals L60-71, _irls L74-84, _place L87-96, rot_consistency L99-111, frame_from/cyl L32-43)
generic_components.what: GT-free axis of a body of revolution. Line-complex IRLS (Pottmann-Randrup) on all points and on 6 k-means clusters, plus PCA axes and the opening direction; the candidates are scored by rotational self-consistency, and near-ties prefer the opening. No object knowledge. normals() is also reused by prim_rack (L58, L607) and prim_boards.
reusable_for: white_pot body (but prim_potlid needed its own pot_axis search: fit_axis gave axes 5-36 deg apart on 3 pot episodes, prim_potlid docstring L310)

generic_components.name: lathe_obs.py: profile + revolve (sector_stat L46-57, smooth_fill L157-163, main L217-285, revolve L166-190)
generic_components.what: View-side classification (outer/inner/cap by the radial view component ±0.3). Per-height-bin sector medians, with a bin kept only if ≥6 of 24 sectors saw it (so a handle or marker drops out). Wall thickness = median(r_out - r_in). Floor rule. Closed profile revolved into a watertight thin-walled mesh. Generic within the class 'container or solid of revolution'; it has no test of whether the object is a body of revolution.
reusable_for: white_pot_lid (dome sheet path in prim_potlid reuses revolve)

generic_components.name: lathe_obs.py appendages (L289-313) / hybrid.py (L3-19)
generic_components.what: Residual parts outside the lathe. lathe_obs voxel-splats points more than app_d outside the profile (2 mm voxels, closing, marching cubes). hybrid.py keeps another mesh's faces lying outside the revolved profile by more than MARGIN (point-in-polygon in (r,h)). Both are object-agnostic but need a lathe body (hybrid reads the .lathe.json). Neither does a boolean union: parts are concatenated, so the output is not a single watertight solid, unlike the manifold3d union in prim_*.
reusable_for: any lathe-body object with appendages: blue_cup, beige_cup, white_pot, water_pitcher

generic_components.name: Marker balls: prim_potlid.clusters L186-199, fit_sphere L203-235, markers_from L238-291; prim_rack.marker_parts L564-584 and the residual step in build L663-672
generic_components.what: Compact residual clusters, sphere fit (free radius or the 7 mm prior from our own stereo), gap-to-body test, and a stem only when points support it. prim_rack adds a curvature/free-radius check. The only object-specific bit is the rack's 'not over the basin' rejection (L673-682).
reusable_for: all objects carrying mocap markers (all 10 scanned objects; spoon unknown)

generic_components.name: Assembly: manifold3d union (prim_potlid.to_mf/from_mf/union L93-104, L609-611; prim_rack.prism/hull/rings L484-494, batch_boolean L539, L689)
generic_components.what: Watertight union of parts, so no hidden internal faces enter the scorer's area sampling. Object-agnostic.

generic_components.name: 2-D section shapes: prim_rack.rrect_sd L163-172, rrect_poly L175-184, view_inplane L187-190, peg_solid L544-561 (lofted convex hull of rings)
generic_components.what: Rounded-rectangle signed distance with gradient, polygon output, in-plane view component, and a loft through elliptic rings. Generic shape kernels; only their use (tray, cup tube, pegs) is rack-specific.
reusable_for: tapered posts and handles on any object

generic_components.name: Table-contact frame: prim_rack.lower_plane L98-120, initial_frame L123-146, to_rack/rotate_frame L149-159, rack_to_object L587-591
generic_components.what: Lower supporting plane of the points (the table cut), long in-plane axis, rigid frame changes. Generic for static objects resting on the table. initial_frame's 'smallest PCA axis = up' assumes a low, elongated object, and the -y 'front = camera side' convention is arbitrary.
reusable_for: mini_dust_pan and wooden boards when lying flat
not tall objects (pitcher, cups standing): smallest PCA axis is horizontal there

generic_components.name: Multi-episode joint fit: prim_rack.icp_align L703-721, mean_rigid L724-730, joint L743-778, JOINT_TOL gate in run L821-828
generic_components.what: Trimmed rigid ICP of each episode's points to a reference, merge, one fit, then the mesh is moved to the mean episode frame. Episodes are admitted only if their own fit's fidelity is ≤1.25× the best. Generic, except that joint() calls the rack-specific lip_above_cut (L761) for the 'up' normals.
reusable_for: any object with ≥2 public episodes: white_pot (8), plastic_dish_rack (5), white_pot_lid (2), blue_cup (2), wooden boards (2); note fusion hurt the blue cup [D] 0.291 single vs 0.396 merged, so this must stay a candidate under selection, not a default

generic_components.name: Candidate/selection driver: prim_rack.fidelity L781-788, run L792-854 (minus the floor-depth pass L796-805)
generic_components.what: Build every variant per episode plus the joint fit, score all of them with obs_fidelity over all episodes' points, pick the minimum, and write candidates.jsonl / selection.json / manifest. Object-agnostic plumbing (OBJ is a constant, L62).
reusable_for: all 11 objects, once a per-object or generic fitter exists

object_specific_rules.name: Rack frame convention and cup-holder end
object_specific_rules.rule: initial_frame L123-146: up = smallest PCA axis turned toward the cameras, refined by the table cut; x = long in-plane axis; cameras on -y. find_cup L194-201: the cup holder is the end holding points above 0.65 × the 99.8 % height. The frame is rotated 180 deg so it sits at -x (fit L600-603).
object_specific_rules.why_needed: Every later step (lip on the bbox edges, tray to the right of x0, pegs right of the cup face, visible-face signs in cup_upright) is written in this fixed frame.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Take up from the table plane obs_points already estimates, and drop the left/right convention by finding parts with a residual-driven decomposition: fit the dominant part, cluster the residual, fit each cluster. A 'tall cluster' then becomes a generic tube/frustum part wherever it is, not 'the cup end'.

object_specific_rules.name: Tray lip model
object_specific_rules.rule: lip_tops L204-219: lip samples are tray points within 12 mm of the bbox front/back/right edges (cup end excluded), the 98th-percentile height per 1 cm segment. rim_height L222-224 takes their median; lip_plane L227-238 fits a tilted plane with 3 mm robust rejection.
object_specific_rules.why_needed: The lip height differs between sides per episode (table-cut tilt, view-dependent tops; docstring L229-230), and the inner-face slope s(h) is parameterised from it.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Fit a generic 'drafted extrusion shell' part whose top cap is fitted, not looked for at bbox edges. Take the outline from an occupancy polygon as prim_boards already does (occupancy -> contour -> simplification).

object_specific_rules.name: Tray = rounded-rectangle frustum minus a sloped basin, pinned to the cup holder
object_specific_rules.rule: fit_outline L241-289: only points with x > x0 + 30 mm are used; the left end is pinned at the cup holder (xa = xl - T_WALL, L610). There are three view-classified point classes with targets: outer sd = so1(H_r - h), inner sd = -(s0 + s1(H_r - h)), lip sd = -s0/2. Bounds: hy 30-150 mm, rc 2-60 mm, s0 4-30 mm, s1 0-1.5, theta ±0.2 rad. build_body L497-541 makes block - basin, with the basin trimmed at the cup face (L519-520, x_cup_face L632).
object_specific_rules.why_needed: The tray floor is never seen and the rack is seen from one side only (28 % scan coverage, README s4), so a closed parametric shell is what fixes the unseen inside and floor.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Make 'rounded-rect or polygon frustum shell with draft and wall t' a library part. Infer its extent from the residual instead of from a named neighbour. Use RANSAC planes (Efficient RANSAC, Schnabel 2007 [L]) for the wall faces, and choose part vs no-part by obs_fidelity plus a parameter-count penalty.

object_specific_rules.name: Unseen tray floor depth
object_specific_rules.rule: Floor = a T_WALL plate on the table (fit L626-627). Its depth is shared across episodes as the deepest table cut: run L796-805 (depth = max lip_above_cut + band - T_WALL), lip_above_cut L733-740.
object_specific_rules.why_needed: obs_points drops the bottom 8 mm (table_band) and the rack never moves, so no episode sees its floor.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: One generic base rule for every static object: whatever lies below the lowest observed point down to the table plane is a closed base of wall thickness t (measured if inner and outer were both seen, otherwise the same prior grid with a 'pass at every value' rule).

object_specific_rules.name: Cup-holder tube
object_specific_rules.rule: fit_cup L360-388: region x < xr + 12 mm; top = median over 2 cm y-bands of the 99th-percentile height; inner floor = up-facing points (n·up > 0.85, ≥ 50 points) inside the cavity. cup_lsq L292-321: rounded-rect tube with lean and draft linear in h, bounds ±0.25. cup_upright L324-357 hard-codes which faces are visible ('Every face the camera can see faces -y or +x here', L328; side tests L333-336). CUP_LEAN default True (L79).
object_specific_rules.why_needed: It is the rack's tallest part and drives registration. The lean was chosen by GT-free fidelity after a first run informed by scan measurements (L80-82, README s9 integrity).
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: The tube fitter itself (cup_lsq with view-classified outer/inner/rim classes) is a reusable 'drafted rounded-rect tube' part. Remove the region rule and the face-sign assumptions; seed it from a residual cluster and keep it only if fidelity improves. Pick lean on/off by fidelity, as the clean-up round already did.

object_specific_rules.name: Peg rows
object_specific_rules.rule: detect_pegs L391-418: a slice 12-35 mm above the cut, inside the basin by ≥ 10 mm and ≥ 6 mm right of the cup face (L636); blobs of 10-150 cells of 2 mm (40-600 mm²); rows = centres with |dy| < 12 mm, ≥ 3 per row. fit_peg_row L421-480: one round tapered template per row (PEG_KAPPA = 1, PEG_LEAN off, knots every 6 mm, centres ±8 mm). A row is accepted only if its top H_p > H_r + 8 mm (L642).
object_specific_rules.why_needed: Pegs are thin, seen from one side only, and repeated; sharing one template per row makes them estimable. A free lean came out 2-22 deg between episodes (L72-73).
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Generic repeated-element detection: cluster residual blobs, test for a row or lattice by transform voting (Pauly et al. 2008 [L]), and share one template (cone / generalized cylinder) across all instances. Set slice heights relative to the fitted body height rather than in absolute mm.

object_specific_rules.name: Marker not over the basin
object_specific_rules.rule: build L673-682: reject a marker candidate whose centre lies inside the tray inner face and right of the cup holder.
object_specific_rules.why_needed: Peg flares and clutter inside the tray passed the sphere tests.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Generic: reject any marker centre inside any fitted cavity or solid (an inside/outside test against the assembled body), with no named basin.

object_specific_rules.name: Pot handle = flat bar reaching > 60 mm beyond the body
object_specific_rules.rule: prim_potlid build_pot L572-578: the handle is the largest residual cluster (≥ 200 points) whose 99th-percentile radius exceeds rmax + 60 mm. bar_handle L461-550 models it as a flat bar with a rounded tip; thickness clip 3-8 mm, else prior 5 mm; a hole is cut if an occupancy gap ≥ 40 mm² lies within 60 mm of the tip.
object_specific_rules.why_needed: Markers and noise also form residual clusters, and 60 mm separates the long handle from them. The flat-bar shape is the pot's actual handle.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Generic appendage step: for each residual cluster, fit {flat bar, swept tube/GC, strap, voxel splat} and keep the best by fidelity. Use a threshold relative to the body radius, or none at all (size and model choice decide).

object_specific_rules.name: Pot axis and open end
object_specific_rules.rule: pot_axis L303-355: a 600-direction hemisphere search scored by rim flatness (rim window 0.6R..R+20 mm) plus rotational consistency. pot_body L366-375: the open end is the end with fewer points near the axis. Polar origin hO = hlo + 0.6 H (L379).
object_specific_rules.why_needed: lathe_obs.fit_axis gave axes 5-36 deg apart on three pot episodes (L310).
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Already nearly generic for open containers. Make it the default axis search for every lathe candidate and let fidelity choose between fit_axis and pot_axis.

object_specific_rules.name: Lid as disc + dome + flange window + arch
object_specific_rules.rule: build_lid L628-746: axis = smallest PCA direction, up = toward the cameras (L631-634); centre by circle fit to per-sector edges; flange window r 40-80 mm (L652); dome = quadratic on r 15-35 mm (lid_top_profile L615-625); underside = top - T_LID (2.5 mm prior, L75). The arch is the first residual cluster with in-plane extent > 50 mm (L730-735), swept as a strap 8-30 mm wide (arch_strap L749-810).
object_specific_rules.why_needed: The lid is seen only from above, so the underside and thickness are priors. The arch hides the centre of the dome.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Express the windows as fractions of the measured edge radius (e.g. 0.5-1.0 R_edge, 0.2-0.45 R_edge) instead of mm. Choose 'disc sheet' vs 'container' from the PCA eigenvalue ratio or by fitting both and comparing fidelity. Treat the arch with the same generic appendage step as the pot handle.

object_specific_rules.name: Lathe-class assumptions (not one object, one family)
object_specific_rules.rule: lathe_obs main: open end = the end with inner-wall evidence (L238-243); t = 3 mm when fewer than 3 bins show both walls (L244); observed floor = a layer < 10 mm thick in the lower 40 % of the height (L255-259); MINSEC 6 of 24 sectors assumes appendages fill ≤ 3 sectors (L227-230).
object_specific_rules.why_needed: These are the priors for unseen floors and interiors of containers.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: Keep them as family priors, but add an applicability gate. Rotational consistency alone does not work: the dust pan scored 2.8 mm vs the blue cup's 2.2 mm [M]. Compare fidelity against the library_v3 baseline instead (rejected the lathe on 4/4 non-lathe objects [M]).

object_specific_rules.name: Which fitter runs on which object
object_specific_rules.rule: There is no dispatcher. prim_rack hard-codes OBJ = 'plastic_dish_rack' (L62), prim_potlid takes 'pot'/'lid' on the CLI (L816), prim_boards takes an object list. The object -> family mapping and each family's part list were decided by hand (by agents per object type, README s9).
object_specific_rules.why_needed: Each fitter's later steps presume its part list.
object_specific_rules.could_be_automated_how: [H] Run every generic family (lathe, slab extrusion, drafted frustum/tube shell, GC sweep, TSDF baseline) on every object and select by obs_fidelity with a complexity penalty. Optionally, a VLM reads the colour crops and proposes a part list (body type, appendage types and counts) that limits which families and counts to try; the VLM only proposes and fidelity decides, since LLMs 'misattribute constraints' (ShapeLib [L]).

audits.lines_generic_vs_specific:
Non-blank, non-comment lines, classified by line range (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/90d4009c-b597-536b-9d55-58f81afca135/scratchpad/audit_auto/count.py; every code line assigned, coverage check passed).

Five audited files, 1,226 lines in total: about 743 generic, 395 object-specific, 88 docstring.
- prim_rack.py: 762 = 323 generic (37+ helpers: load, lower_plane, frame, rrect kernels, prism/hull, marker_parts, build plumbing, ICP/joint, fidelity, run driver, CLI) + 395 rack-specific (find_cup, lip_*, fit_outline, cup_lsq/cup_upright/fit_cup, detect_pegs, fit_peg_row, build_body, peg_solid, fit, in-basin marker rule, lip_above_cut, floor-depth pass, rack constants) + 44 docstring. That is about 45 % generic and 55 % specific of its code.
- lathe_obs.py: 264 code + 19 doc. All generic, but only for the body-of-revolution family.
- obs_points.py: 123 + 16 doc, generic.
- obs_fidelity.py: 17 + 7 doc, generic.
- hybrid.py: 16 + 2 doc, generic but lathe-only.

Dependency prim_potlid.py (not one of the five): 727 = 218 generic (utilities, clusters, fit_sphere, markers_from, union, residual_mask) + 469 pot/lid-specific + 40 doc, so about 32 % generic.

Approximations: initial_frame was counted as generic although it assumes a low, elongated object; joint() was counted as generic although it calls the rack-specific lip_above_cut.

Bottom line: each specialised fitter is roughly one third to one half reusable plumbing and one half to two thirds hand-written object knowledge. The point extraction, the lathe family and the selector need no per-object code.
new_object_failure_modes: [M] prim_rack.py build on the mini dust pan (ep39) crashes after 7 s: IndexError in fit_outline L248. find_cup L194 labels the dust pan's tall points as the 'cup holder', and the selection x > x0 + 30 mm (the tray to its right) is empty.

[M] prim_rack.py build on the water pitcher (ep22, 57 s) and the mini sweeper (ep31, 4 s) exit 0 and write watertight meshes (802 and 640 faces), but the parameters sit on their bounds. Pitcher: tray hy = 30.0 mm (lower bound), rc = 2.0 mm (lower bound), a 400 mm-long 'tray' (hx 200 mm), 0 inner-face points, cup ex = 80 mm (upper bound). Sweeper: hy 30.0 mm, s0 4.0 mm (both lower bounds), all four cup lean/draft parameters at ±0.25. Nothing inside the fitter says 'this model does not apply'. Only the downstream fidelity flags it: pitcher 48.85 mm vs library_v3 7.05 mm; sweeper 11.30 vs 4.22 mm (sum_mm, lower is better).

[M] lathe_obs.py never refuses. It exits 0 with a mesh on the dust pan (13 s), pitcher (20 s), sweeper (8 s) and rack (11 s). Rotational self-consistency was 2.8 / 10.1 / 4.3 / 18.4 mm vs 2.2 mm on the blue cup ep21, so the dust pan (a sheet, not a body of revolution) scores almost like a cup: rot_consistency is not a usable 'is this a body of revolution' gate. Three of the four fell back to the 3 mm default wall (L244).

[M] obs_fidelity against our own library_v3 meshes rejected every wrong-family lathe: dust pan 5.98 vs 3.64 mm, pitcher 7.91 vs 7.05, sweeper 10.29 vs 4.22, rack 11.31 vs 8.55. It accepted the right one on the blue cup ep21: 4.10 vs 6.07, consistent with the existing [D] 0.523 -> 0.291 cm. All single-episode points. The pitcher margin is the narrowest (0.86 mm), and these are 5 cases only.

[M] On the pitcher, 221,617 of 250,235 downsampled points (89 %) lie more than 4 mm outside the fitted lathe and are voxel-splatted (lathe_obs L289-313). The 'lathe' mesh is mostly a voxel splat around a 136 mm-high body (rmax 52.7 mm). Handle and spout break the 6-of-24-sector rule (L227-230) and pull the axis (rotcons 10.1 mm).

[E, code reading] prim_potlid on a new object: the pot handle rule (largest residual cluster reaching > 60 mm beyond the body, L577) would pick a pitcher handle, but bar_handle models a straight flat bar, not a loop. The lid path's absolute-mm windows (flange r 40-80 mm L652, dome r 15-35 mm L615, arch extent > 50 mm L733) assume this lid's size, so another disc of a different size would fit the wrong annulus. Not run.

[E, code reading] prim_rack.initial_frame (L124-129) takes the smallest PCA axis as 'up'. That holds for a low, long, static object; for anything tall (pitcher, standing cups) it is horizontal, and the lower-plane refinement then fits the wrong 'table'. This matches the nonsense pitcher fit above.

[M] obs_fidelity.py documents --icp 1 and --trim but implements neither: line 10 drops only the flag tokens, and the value is then read as a mesh path (crash: 'string is not a file: 0.5'). Any mesh not already in our track frame (generated meshes, a new template) would be scored unaligned. An automated pipeline needs an alignment step before this selector.

[E] obs_points is generic but cannot fix upstream errors. A wrong track (beige cup ep11 frame 0, board identity in ep23, README s4/s9) gives wrong points. The 8 mm table band and static poses (rack) leave every base unseen, so every family needs a base/thickness prior, and obs_fidelity is biased toward thin sheets there.

[E] hybrid.py and lathe_obs appendages concatenate parts without a boolean union, so the output is not watertight and may hold internal faces. The prim_* fitters avoid this with manifold3d because the scorer area-samples surfaces.
audits.summary:
Answer to the owner: partly case by case. There are four bespoke fitters: prim_potlid (pot + lid), prim_rack and prim_boards. Each has a part list and part-finding rules written by hand (by agents, per object type), plus mm-sized bounds and priors for unseen geometry. Examples: the rack's 'cup holder = tall end' (find_cup L194), lip at the bbox edges (L204), a tray pinned to the cup holder (L241, L610), peg rows from a 12-35 mm slice (L391) and a floor plate on the table (L626, L796). The pot handle is the cluster 'reaching > 60 mm beyond the body' (prim_potlid L577); the lid uses r 40-80 mm flange and 15-35 mm dome windows (L652, L615).

Once a fitter exists, everything runs automatically and GT-free: no per-episode settings, shared parameters, and selection by obs_fidelity. Much of the plumbing is generic. obs_points (all objects), obs_fidelity (all objects), the marker-ball fitter, manifold3d union, ICP/joint fitting and the candidate driver need no per-object code. lathe_obs is a general method for any body of revolution: cups, the pot body, the lid, and the pitcher body only partly. Line count over the five files: about 743 generic vs 395 object-specific (all in prim_rack, about 55 % of it); prim_potlid is about 32 % generic.

Probes run here [M], GT-free, outputs in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/90d4009c-b597-536b-9d55-58f81afca135/scratchpad/audit_auto/:
- prim_rack crashes on the dust pan (fit_outline L248).
- On the pitcher and sweeper it silently returns watertight nonsense with parameters on their bounds.
- lathe_obs never refuses, and its rotational consistency cannot tell the dust pan (2.8 mm) from a cup (2.2 mm).
- obs_fidelity against the library_v3 baseline rejected all 6 wrong-family meshes and accepted the lathe where it is right (blue cup 4.10 vs 6.07 mm).
- obs_fidelity's documented --icp/--trim flags are unimplemented and crash if used.

Automated path:
- [H1] A fixed library of about 5 generic part families (lathe, slab extrusion, drafted rounded-rect frustum/tube shell, swept generalized cylinder, marker sphere), plus residual-driven decomposition (fit the dominant part, cluster the residual, fit each cluster with every family), plus selection by obs_fidelity with a complexity penalty against the TSDF baseline. No per-object code. Falsified if, run blind on the 10 public objects, it picks a different family from the hand choice on more than 2 objects, or if a pre-registered [D] round shows it is not better than library_v3 on at least 6 of 10.
- [H2] Relative thresholds (fractions of the measured body radius or height) can replace absolute mm windows. Falsified if the relative version changes the selected pot/lid/rack meshes' fidelity by more than 5 %.
- [H3] A VLM part list from the colour crops only narrows the search; the VLM proposes and fidelity decides (ShapeLib: LLMs misattribute constraints [L]). Falsified if its part lists disagree with the hand-written ones on at least 3 of 9 public objects.
- [L] Efficient RANSAC (Schnabel 2007) and repeated-element detection (Pauly 2008) cover the plane, cylinder, cone and peg-row cases.

Two caveats stay:
- Unseen bases and thicknesses still need priors, tested on a grid and kept only if the result holds at every value, and obs_fidelity is biased toward thin sheets there.
- Bad tracks (beige cup ep11, board ep23) defeat any fitter.

methods.name: Efficient RANSAC shape detection (Schnabel, Wahl, Klein)
methods.source: Computer Graphics Forum 26(2); preprint read in full
methods.url: https://www.hinkali.com/Education/PointCloud.pdf (preprint mirror; the Bonn link https://cg.cs.uni-bonn.de/backend/v1/files/publications/schnabel-2007-efficient.pdf now serves a JS app, not the PDF)
methods.code_url: Authors' library: research-only (https://armarx.humanoids.kit.edu/d8/daf/ReadMe_8txt.html). Reimplementation: CGAL Shape_detection https://doc.cgal.org/latest/Shape_detection/
methods.licence: Authors' code: research-only. CGAL: GPL-3+ or a commercial licence from GeometryFactory (the CGAL 6.2 reference marks the package GPL)
methods.cpu_feasible: Yes. [L] 0.4-1.9 M points in about 10-60 s on 2007 hardware (Table 1); the abstract says 'several millions of samples within less than a minute'. [M] My simplified single-thread numpy re-implementation took 4-81 s per object on 13k-128k points (2 mm voxels).
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: [L] Real laser scans with registration errors work for large shapes. On synthetic noise, detection 'starts to become unstable' above 20 % noise; at sigma = 1 % of the bbox diagonal, 'small or very narrow shapes (e.g. some of the screw heads) can no longer be reliably segmented'. [M] Probe on OUR points (eps 2 mm, alpha 25 deg, 2 mm voxels): it explained 24-60 % of points (sweeper 0.24, rack 0.26, dust pan 0.34, pot 0.35, pitcher 0.37, lid 0.48, blue cup 0.50, board 1 0.60), using 8-83 disconnected patches per object. Loosened (eps 3 mm, 40 mm sampling radius): pot 0.42, cup 0.57, board 1 0.65. A marker-ball pass (1 mm voxels, sphere r 2.5-6.5 mm on the residual) returned 75 spheres on the lid, 35 on board 1 and 64 on the pitcher, so mostly false positives [E].
methods.output: A point-to-primitive assignment plus unbounded shape parameters (plane, sphere, cylinder, cone, torus) and a residual set. No bounded patches, no watertight solids, no thickness.
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Usable only as a proposal front end. On our 1-2 mm stereo noise it splits curved bodies into dozens of fragments and invents small spheres. Handles come out as torus or cylinder fragments; the lid arch as plane or cylinder pieces; rack pegs as small cones only if each has min_pts support; marker balls are unreliable unless the body model is subtracted first and a stand-off rule applied, which is what prim_potlid already does.
methods.reported_accuracy: [L] Synthetic sphere parameters recovered with 10 % noise and 80 % outliers; up to 95 % outliers tolerated at 2 % noise.

methods.name: CGAL Region Growing shape detection (after Lafarge and Mallet)
methods.cpu_feasible: Yes. [L] 300k / 600k / 900k / 1.2 M points in 0.76 / 1.69 / 2.80 / 4.06 s (3D, k-NN). Deterministic, unlike RANSAC.
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: [L] Shown on scenes. No published evidence at small-object scale with 1-2 mm stereo noise. Smoothness-based growing tends to merge parts across smooth blends (handle to body) [E].
methods.output: Regions of points: planes, spheres and cylinders on 3D point sets in 6.x. Older 4.x versions grew planes only. No solids.
methods.fit_to_our_problem: A cheap, repeatable segmentation of planar parts (boards, dust-pan faces, rack tray walls) and of cylinders and pegs. It does not handle surfaces of revolution, sweeps or thickness.
methods.reported_accuracy: Runtime only; no accuracy benchmark in the manual

methods.name: pyransac3d
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: No published evaluation. The documented API returns one best model per call and does not mention normals [L].
methods.output: One primitive per call: plane, cylinder, cuboid, sphere, line, circle or point, with its inliers
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Weaker than Schnabel-style detection: no normals, no localized sampling, no multi-shape extraction. Trivial to reimplement in our own code.

methods.name: PCL sample consensus models and region growing (Rabbani-style)
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: Widely used on Kinect-class data, but I found no small-object accuracy figure. The torus model's status conflicts between doc versions ('not implemented' vs implemented).
methods.output: Single-model RANSAC (plane, sphere, cylinder, cone, circle, ...) and smoothness region growing; no solids
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Same role as CGAL with a permissive licence, but needs a C++ build. Nothing in it beats a numpy reimplementation for our scale.

methods.name: Open3D planar patch detection (Araujo and Oliveira, robust-statistics planes)
methods.cpu_feasible: Yes, O(n log n) octree split-and-merge (secondary source)
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: [L-abs] Parameters adapt to the local sample distribution; planes only
methods.output: Planar patches (oriented boxes)
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Boards and dust-pan faces only

methods.name: GlobFit: consistently fitting primitives by discovering global relations (Li, Wu, Chrysanthou, Sharf, Cohen-Or, Mitra)
methods.cpu_feasible: Yes (C++ with constrained optimisation). Runtime not verified.
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: [L-abs] Designed for noisy, incomplete scans of man-made objects; tested on synthetic and scanned data with noise, outliers and non-uniform sampling. Wu et al. 2018 report that on a poor-quality real scan GlobFit extracted 'only a limited number of surface patches'.
methods.output: RANSAC primitives (planes, cylinders, cones, spheres) refined under learned relations (parallel and orthogonal orientation, coaxial or coplanar placement, equal radii). Patches, not solids.
methods.fit_to_our_problem: The idea is worth copying by parameter sharing in our own fitters: equal radii and parallel axes for the rack's 2x6 pegs, equal marker-ball radius, C2-symmetric pot handles, coaxial lid knob. The code itself cannot go into a submission.
methods.reported_accuracy: Qualitative plus some ground-truth comparisons (numbers not read)

methods.name: RAPter / CGAL Shape Regularization (planar regularity)
methods.licence: RAPter Apache-2.0 (LICENSE read). CGAL Shape_regularization GPL [E].
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: Real building and indoor scans; planes only
methods.output: Regularised planes (parallel, orthogonal, coplanar)
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Planes only: boards and the dust pan at most

methods.name: Kinetic Shape Reconstruction (Bauchet and Lafarge) in CGAL 6.0+
methods.cpu_feasible: Yes (C++). Jiang et al. 2023 measured 570 s on their 'Cheese' model.
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: [L] Detected planes go into a kinetic partition, then a min-cut inside/outside labelling. The 6.1 manual adds a ground option for clouds that do not close the model from below. On a curved CAD model Jiang et al. 2023 measured KSR at SMH 169.44 % against 2.45 % for primitive assembly.
methods.output: A watertight polygonal mesh
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Planar objects only (boards, perhaps the dust pan or rack tray). Unseen undersides get closed by the ground or bounding box. It fails on curved bodies. Our board problems are track identity and registration flips, not representation.
methods.reported_accuracy: [L] SMH 169 % on a curved CAD model (Jiang 2023, Table 2)

methods.name: PolyFit / CGAL Polygonal Surface Reconstruction
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: Real building scans; planar only
methods.output: A watertight polygonal surface
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Boards only; KSR covers the same ground

methods.name: COMPOD: concise plane arrangements (Sulzer and Lafarge)
methods.licence: LICENSE file reads 'Contact INRIA for licensing questions' (not open)
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: Planes from LiDAR; interior/exterior labelling from normals or a reference mesh
methods.output: Low-poly watertight mesh or convex decomposition
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Planar only, and the licence is unclear

methods.name: Completion and reconstruction with primitive shapes (Schnabel, Degener, Klein)
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: [L-abs] Built for incomplete point clouds: detected primitives guide a closed-mesh reconstruction, extend the surrounding structure into holes and create edges and corners where primitives meet. A later survey says its completions follow CAD-like shapes.
methods.output: A closed mesh plus an idealised CAD model
methods.fit_to_our_problem: The right idea for closing never-seen undersides (extend the fitted wall or plane, then cap). There is no code, and it does not create double-sided thin walls.

methods.name: Structure-aware surface reconstruction via primitive assembly (Jiang et al.)
methods.code_url: None in the paper; it uses Gurobi
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: [L] CAD models with synthetic Gaussian noise up to sigma = 0.04 of the bounding radius and progressive erasure ('occlusion'). Authors' limitation: 'inadequate primitive extraction due to severe occlusion or noise can degrade the quality'.
methods.output: A manifold watertight surface assembled from plane, cylinder, sphere, cone and torus patches (binary linear programming)
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Evidence that automated detection plus assembly into watertight solids works on CAD-like data. It is single-surface (no wall thickness), has no code and needs Gurobi.
methods.reported_accuracy: [L] SMH 2.45 % vs iPSR 4.23, DSE 3.15, SIREN 41.79, KSR 169.44 (Cheese model)

methods.name: Constructing 3D CSG models from raw point clouds (Wu, Xu, Wang)
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: [L] The most relevant real-data evidence: on a Kinect scan with 'significant structured noise and data deficiency' it infers missing structure 'to some extent; however, the dimensional information is false due to these incomplete or corrupted surface patches'. It needs GlobFit patches as input and correct patch orientation, and fails on free-form surfaces.
methods.output: A CSG tree of bounded primitives (cuboid, cylinder, cone, sphere, torus). Selection by binary optimisation with an MDL-style error-plus-complexity objective. Watertight solids.
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Closest published analogue of an automated kit-of-parts with MDL selection. It shows structure can be automated while dimensions on Kinect-class data stay wrong, so a dense refit to observations (what we do) is still required.

methods.name: InverseCSG (Du et al.)
methods.code_url: The project page's 'Code' link points to the ACM DL entry; no repo located
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: Built for clean CAD meshes; no noisy or partial evidence
methods.output: CSG program (solid)
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Needs clean, complete input
methods.reported_accuracy: Compactness and runtime vs prior CSG methods

methods.name: Evolutionary CSG tree extraction (Fayolle and Pasko 2016; Friedrich et al. GECCO 2019) and the 2023 CSG survey
methods.cpu_feasible: Evolutionary search is slow by the survey's own account
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: Primitive fitting is borrowed from RANSAC-type methods; no small-object real evidence found
methods.output: CSG solids
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Background only

methods.name: EMS: probabilistic superquadric recovery (Liu, Wu, Ruan, Chirikjian)
methods.code_url: https://github.com/bmlklwx/EMS-superquadric_fitting (MATLAB and Python with numba; Python multi-SQ demo added)
methods.licence: No LICENSE file in the repo (checked LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt on main and master). Python setup.py declares the 'MIT' classifier: ambiguous, treat as unlicensed until the authors confirm.
methods.cpu_feasible: Yes. The Python port is about 3-5x faster than MATLAB; runtimes appear only in plots [L]. Seconds per object [E].
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: [L] Real tests are KIT (laser, near-complete models, 97 objects, about 1500 points) and BigBIRD (PrimeSense, 91 objects, about 1000 points), each restricted to objects a single superquadric fits. Partial-view tests are synthetic (partial ratio 1.0 to 0.2). The multi-SQ extension 'requires the object ... possesses an inherent hierarchical geometric structure'.
methods.output: Closed superquadric solids, single or hierarchical. No hollow or thin-walled shapes.
methods.fit_to_our_problem: It cannot represent cup or pot cavities, thin lids or fins. Handles are toroidal and fit badly. Worth copying: the Gaussian-uniform outlier model and the 'switching' step. A possible blob-part fitter for the sweeper's bristle block.
methods.reported_accuracy: [L] Beats baselines on KIT and BigBIRD (plots only)

methods.name: Marching-Primitives (Liu, Wu, Ruan, Chirikjian)
methods.cpu_feasible: MATLAB plus Image Processing Toolbox only ('Python implementation is planned', Mar 2023); 6.7 s per object [L, previous review]
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: It needs a full signed distance field on a voxel grid (the README makes meshes watertight first). SuperFlex (2026) notes that SDF-based methods like this one and Light-SQ are limited in real settings where only partial point clouds exist [L].
methods.output: A set of superquadric solids
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Our TSDF has no reliable sign in never-seen regions (undersides, interiors), and the outputs are solid blobs. Needs MATLAB.

methods.name: Nonparametric Bayesian superquadric abstraction (Wu, Liu, Ruan, Chirikjian)
methods.code_url: None found (Papers with Code lists none)
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: Not verified
methods.output: Superquadric set; the number of primitives is inferred automatically (Dirichlet-process style)
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Automatic count selection is relevant in principle; the solid-blob limitation still applies

methods.name: Superquadric decomposition via geometric-aware inlier refinement (Rinaldi et al.)
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: [L-abs] 'Synthetic and real' data, not named; graph-cut inlier refinement with normal-consistency priors for adjacent primitives
methods.output: Superquadric set
methods.fit_to_our_problem: The graph-cut reassignment of points between adjacent parts (handle vs body) is a transferable idea; the solid-blob limitation remains
methods.reported_accuracy: Claims gains over RANSAC-based methods (no numbers on the abstract page)

methods.name: SuperDec (ICCV 2025) and SuperFlex (arXiv 2607.01015, Jul 2026)
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: SuperFlex claims robustness to partial real point clouds via a trained model
methods.output: Superquadric sets (SuperFlex adds bending and tapering)
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Learned (out of scope: no learning, no third-party weights). Solid blobs.

methods.name: Recover-and-select / MDL model selection for range data (Leonardis, Gupta, Bajcsy; Leonardis, Solina, Jaklic)
methods.cpu_feasible: Yes: generate an over-complete set of part hypotheses, then a quadratic boolean selection
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: Real range images (1990s), single view
methods.output: Selected set of parametric models (surfaces or superquadrics)
methods.fit_to_our_problem: The principle to automate 'which parts': grow candidate parts from seeds on our points (lathe shell, plate, tube, peg, ball), then select the subset that best trades points explained against parameter cost. Our obs_fidelity selector is the 'select' half without a complexity term.

methods.name: Geometric AIC / geometric MDL (Kanatani) and GRIC (Torr) for primitive-type selection
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: [L-abs] For geometric fitting the noise level, not the number of points, is the asymptotic variable; G-AIC and G-MDL behave differently in detecting degeneracy
methods.output: A score per candidate model
methods.fit_to_our_problem: A principled penalty for choosing cylinder vs cone vs free profile vs plate when the stereo noise sigma (about 1-2 mm) is known. It replaces hand thresholds such as the lathe gate MAD <= 3 mm. Caveat: our noise is structured (double layers, edge bleeding), not Gaussian [E].

methods.name: Label-cost multi-model fitting: PEARL (Isack and Boykov 2012), Multi-X (Barath and Matas 2018), Progressive-X (ICCV 2019)
methods.licence: Progressive-X MIT (LICENSE read); Multi-X only on an unlicensed Gitee mirror
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: [L] Multi-X fits planes and cylinders jointly on real LiDAR (traffic signs, balusters). Progressive-X's released examples cover homographies, F/E, 6D poses and vanishing points, not 3D primitives.
methods.output: Point labelling plus model instances (MDL-like label costs)
methods.fit_to_our_problem: An energy formulation for automated multi-part selection. Our part types (lathe shells, sweeps) would need custom model classes, so writing the energy ourselves is simpler.
methods.reported_accuracy: Beats T-Linkage and RPA on their benchmarks [L-abs]

methods.name: Slippage analysis for kinematic-surface segmentation (Gelfand and Guibas)
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: [L] Scanned mechanical parts. Schnabel 2007 calls it costly and 'sensitive to noise'.
