key_insights: Answer to the owner's question [E]: yes, the current good meshes are made case by case. An agent wrote each object type's part list and fitting rules: lathe_obs.py for cups, prim_potlid.py for the pot and lid, prim_rack.py, prim_boards.py. All parameters are then fitted to our points and the final pick is made by the GT-free selector, both automatically. What is still manual is the structure: which parts, how many, and how they connect.

The classical literature does have an automated pipeline (detect, relate, select, solidify) [L]: (1) Efficient RANSAC or region growing proposes primitives; (2) GlobFit-style relations share parameters; (3) MDL or recover-and-select picks the subset (Leonardis 1995; Wu, Xu, Wang 2018; Zhou 2015); (4) inside/outside labelling assembles watertight solids (Schnabel 2009, KSR, Jiang 2023, Wu 2018 CSG). All of it is shown on CAD, mechanical or architectural data. On a real Kinect-quality scan, Wu 2018 recovers the structure, but the 'dimensional information is false' [L]. Structure can be automated; the dimensions still need a dense refit to our observations, which our fitters already do.

Measured on our own points [M]: a simplified Schnabel-style RANSAC (plane, sphere, cylinder, cone; eps 2 mm; 2 mm voxels) explains 24-60 % of points with 8-83 disconnected patches per object (sweeper 0.24, rack 0.26, dust pan 0.34, pot 0.35, pitcher 0.37, lid 0.48, blue cup 0.50, board 1 0.60), in 7-94 s per object on one CPU thread. Loosened to eps 3 mm it gives pot 0.42, cup 0.57, board 0.65. With one watertight model each, the hand-built kit meshes explain 50 / 72 / 70 / 44 % (pot / lid / board 1 / rack) of the same voxelised points within 2 mm, and 66 / 83 / 84 / 60 % within 3 mm. The criteria differ (RANSAC also tests normals and connectivity), so this is indicative, not a like-for-like comparison. The noise floor is real: pot points sit 1.9 mm median, 6.6 mm p90 from the scan [D, quoted from README section 4].

Marker balls cannot be found generically [M]: a small-sphere pass on the RANSAC residual returned 75 'balls' on the lid, 35 on board 1 and 64 on the pitcher, against a handful of physical markers [E]. A cap-angle test did not separate them (72 of 75 on the lid had cap > 60 deg), because stereo normals at 1 mm are too noisy. Markers need the body model subtracted first and a stand-off and cluster rule, which is what prim_potlid already does. Schnabel's own noise experiment says the same about small or narrow shapes [L].

No classical method I found outputs watertight THIN-WALLED (double-sided) solids from one-sided partial views [L]. Detection methods output point assignments or unbounded patches. Solid methods (Schnabel 2009, KSR, PolyFit, Jiang 2023, Wu 2018, Labatut 2009) close unseen regions with a solid fill, a minimal-area surface or a ground plane. Thickness has to come from a prior or from places where both sides were seen; Ummenhofer and Brox 2013 handles only two-sided thin objects. The offset-shell step (manifold3d or CadQuery shell) has to be ours.

Superquadric methods are the wrong final representation [L]. EMS's real tests are near-complete fused models (KIT laser, BigBIRD PrimeSense, about 1000-1500 points, single-SQ objects only); its partial-view tests are synthetic. Marching-Primitives needs a full signed SDF (MATLAB only, Python 'planned' since Mar 2023). Neither can be hollow. They are at most a blob-part fitter (sweeper bristle block); the EMS outlier model and switching step are the ideas worth copying.

Free-space and visibility consistency (Thrun-Wegbreit 2005, Bohg 2011, Merrell 2007) is the classical cure for 'unseen surface counted as error'. Our obs_all npz already store per-voxel hit and free votes [M]. The kit meshes put 91-96 % of their area in hit voxels, 1-3 % in observed free space and 1-7.5 % in never-observed voxels for pot, lid and board 1. For the rack, 62.7 % of the area is in never-observed voxels and 5.1 % in free space. So a free-space-aware selector would mainly change rack decisions. At 4 mm voxels it cannot measure 1.5-4 mm wall thickness, so it will not fix the thin-sheet bias at the thickness level [M/E].

The realistic automation [H]: replace per-object scripts with one typed part grammar of about 7 part types: lathe shell, plate or extrusion, swept tube or torus arc, peg (cone or cylinder) with lattice, marker sphere on a stem, rounded box or superquadric blob, and free-form residual taken from observations or TSDF. Fill it by iterative recover-and-select: fit the dominant body first (line-complex or slippage type test on the largest segment), then propose parts from the residual (RANSAC or region-growing seeds, slippage type labels, GlobFit-style shared parameters), and select by obs_fidelity + a free-space term + a Kanatani/GRIC complexity penalty with sigma about 1.5 mm. Object names may bias the grammar (they are allowed inputs). Falsifier: run it blind on the 9 public objects. It must reach GT-free fidelity within 0.2 mm of the hand-built pot, lid and rack fits, and, in a later pre-registered [D] round, CD-O within 0.02 cm of them; otherwise per-object templates stay.

Where automation would pay first [E]: objects with no fitter yet, namely the dust pan (planes plus shell; RANSAC found 2 planes covering only 7 % of its points [M]), the sweeper (block plus ring handle) and the pitcher (lathe plus handle plus spout), and later eval-time robustness. For the pot, lid and rack, automation would mostly reproduce what the hand-built fitters already do.

Licence map for anything that might enter submitted code [L, LICENSE files read where stated]. Permissive: pyransac3d Apache-2.0, PCL BSD-3, Open3D MIT, Progressive-X MIT, SymSeg BSD-3, mirror_objects BSD-3, Marching-Primitives MIT, RAPter Apache-2.0. Copyleft: CGAL GPL-3 (Shape detection, KSR, PSR), TreeQSM and Romanengo GPL-3, OpenMVS AGPL-3. Restricted or unclear: GlobFit research-only; COMPOD 'contact INRIA'; EMS has no LICENSE file (setup.py says MIT).
top_claims_to_verify: Claim 1 [M, simplified implementation]: generic primitive RANSAC explains only 24-60 % (eps 2 mm) or 42-65 % (eps 3 mm) of our observed points and splits curved bodies into 8-83 patches. Check: run CGAL 6.x Efficient RANSAC (GPL, local use only) on the same obs clouds (scratchpad obs_all/ep41_white_pot.npz, obs/ep21_blue_cup.npz, obs_all/ep2_white_pot_lid.npz) with camera-oriented PCA normals, eps 2-3 mm. If it explains at least 85 % with at most 15 shapes on the pot and cup, a generic detection front end is viable and the 'needs a body-first grammar' conclusion is wrong. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/90d4009c-b597-536b-9d55-58f81afca135/scratchpad/probe_ransac/probe_ransac.py; outputs run1.jsonl and run2.jsonl in the same folder.

Claim 2 [L]: no published classical method outputs watertight double-sided thin-walled solids from one-sided partial views. Every solid-producing method (Schnabel 2009, KSR, PolyFit, Jiang ICCV 2023, Wu SGP 2018, Labatut 2009) fills unseen regions with a solid, minimal or ground closure. A skeptic should search for 'shell' or 'offset-surface' primitive fitting from single-sided scans. One with code and real-scan results would replace our hand-written shell step.

Claim 3 [M]: the free-space grid in obs_all (4 mm voxels) puts 91-96 % of kit-mesh area in hit voxels and only 1-3 % in free space for pot, lid and board, but leaves 62.7 % of the rack mesh in never-observed voxels. A free-space term therefore cannot resolve wall thickness and will mostly change rack decisions. Check: recompute hit and free votes at 1-2 mm with obs_points.py --vox and re-measure. If lid and rack-floor thickness become measurable, the thin-sheet bias of obs_fidelity is fixable GT-free and the thickness grid-sweep rule can be dropped.

Claim 4 [M]: generic small-sphere detection on our stereo is mostly false positives (75 on the lid, 35 on board 1, 64 on the pitcher). Check: overlay these sphere centres (re-run probe_ransac.py with the pass-2 centres printed) on the colour crops in scratchpad/crops. If most coincide with real mocap balls, marker detection can be generic, and one per-object rule set goes away.

Claim 5 [L]: on real Kinect-quality scans, MDL-selected CSG assemblies recover the structure but get dimensions wrong (Wu, Xu, Wang 2018, Fig. 12 and limitations), and EMS has only been validated on near-complete real clouds (KIT and BigBIRD, about 1000-1500 points). Check by reading Wu 2018 section 5 and EMS section 4.2, or by running EMS on one-sided sweeper-block points from obs/ep31_mini_sweeper.npz (GT-free: compare the fitted extent with the observed silhouette). If either recovers unseen extent within 2 mm, automatic primitive selection could also set dimensions, and a pure-detection pipeline becomes competitive with the hand-built fitters.
open_questions: Owner decision: is GPL-3 code (CGAL Shape detection, KSR) acceptable in the repo shared with the organisers, or must the automated pipeline stay permissive-only (our numpy plus manifold3d)? AGPL (OpenMVS) and research-only (GlobFit) code are effectively excluded either way.

Owner decision: what counts as 'automated'? A typed part grammar biased by the object name (allowed by the rules) is still category-specific; a grammar with no name input is harder and riskier. Which one does the owner want?

Can wall thickness be measured anywhere in our data without GT? For example the rim width seen from above, or edge-on views of the lid rim. If so, the shell step can be fully automatic; if not, thickness stays a grid-swept prior (the existing 1.5 / 2.5 / 4.0 mm rule).

Do the hidden eval scans carry the same marker balls on stems as the public scans? They are physical objects, so probably yes [E]. This decides whether an automatic marker detector is worth building, given that markers shift the area-weighted RMS-radius scale.

Would a pre-registered [D] round accept a free-space-aware selector (obs_fidelity + free-space violation + complexity penalty) evaluated on the existing 32 pot candidates and the rack candidates, before any new fitter is written?

For the objects without a fitter (dust pan, sweeper, pitcher), is the faster route the automated grammar or three more hand-designed fitters? The probe suggests generic detection alone explains only 24-37 % of their points [M].

checked.claim: Efficient RANSAC speed: the abstract says 'several millions of samples within less than a minute'; Table 1 shows 0.4-1.9 M points in about 10-60 s

checked.correction: Confirmed [L]. Table 1 lists 379k-1,922k points in 10.7-61.5 s. The large models (house, church, choir screen) are building laser scans, not small objects.

checked.claim: Efficient RANSAC on noise: it 'starts to become unstable' above 20 % noise; at sigma = 1 % of the bbox diagonal, small or narrow shapes such as screw heads are lost; spheres are recovered at 10 % noise with 80 % outliers, and up to 95 % outliers are tolerated at 2 % noise
checked.how_checked: Read section 5.1, Fig. 5 and Table 2 in the same PDF text
checked.correction: The quotes are accurate [L], but the two noise figures use different units. The '20 %' and '10 %' are sigma as a percentage of the sphere diameter (sphere-octant test). The screw-head failure is at sigma = 1 % of the oil pump's bbox diagonal. Our 1-2 mm stereo noise is about 1 % of a 150-300 mm object diagonal [E], which is exactly where the paper says small or narrow shapes are lost: marker balls, rack pegs, handles.

checked.how_checked: mlanthology ECCV 1994 page; dblp/abstract snippets for IJCV 14(3):253-277 (DOI 10.1007/BF01679685). Full texts were unreachable (UPenn 403).
checked.correction: The ECCV 1994 authors are Leonardis, Solina and Macerl; Jaklic is on the 1997 TPAMI paper. The abstracts confirm the method: seeds, variable-order bivariate polynomials grown by iterative regression, selection as a quadratic Boolean problem solved by winner-takes-all, and 'simplest overall description' for the superquadric version. Whether the 1995 IJCV paper is explicitly MDL, and the 'real single-view range images' claim, could not be verified. The principle is sound, but the paper offers no evidence on noisy partial stereo.

checked.claim: Our obs_fidelity selector is the 'select' half of recover-and-select without a complexity term
checked.how_checked: Read docs/research/mesh-2026-10-26/scripts/obs_fidelity.py
checked.correction: Correct: it uses trimmed mean distances in both directions and no parameter count. Two caveats. (1) The mesh-to-obs term already penalises extra surface inside the observed bbox, which is an implicit complexity penalty. (2) A complexity term would not remove its known thin-sheet bias [E], because unseen undersides add no data cost to either a thin or a thick candidate.

checked.claim: G-AIC / G-MDL (Kanatani TPAMI 2004): the noise level, not the point count, is the asymptotic variable; the two criteria behave differently in detecting degeneracy
checked.how_checked: Downloaded iim.cs.tut.ac.jp/member/kanatani/papers/pamodel2.pdf. Read the abstract, eq. 20 (G-AIC = J + 2(Nd+p)eps^2) and section 8.3 (eps known, or estimated from the general model by eq. 45)
checked.correction: Accurate [L]. Note the framework's assumptions: independent Gaussian errors per point, eps estimated from a general model assumed true, and use for detecting nested degeneracy.

checked.claim: G-AIC/G-MDL (verdict adopt) gives a principled cylinder vs cone vs free-profile vs plate choice from the known 1-2 mm sigma and can replace hand thresholds such as the lathe gate MAD <= 3 mm
checked.how_checked: [M] New GT-free probe scratchpad/verify_probe/gaic_slip_probe.py (reads only obs pts/cam; output verify_probe/run1.jsonl; 76 s CPU). Boards ep24/ep23 wooden_piece_1: largest face, plane (p=3) vs quadratic (6) vs cubic (10) height field. Blue cup ep21/ep22: outer wall, axis fixed from a cylinder fit, cylinder (5) vs cone (6) vs degree-4 r(h) (9). Each at 1/2/4/8 mm voxels.
checked.correction: [M] With eps estimated per eq. 45, G-AIC picks the most flexible model at every voxel size on all 4 clouds, even when the RMS gain is 0.01-0.03 mm (board ep24: plane 1.665 vs cubic 1.649 mm). Delta-J/eps^2 grows with N: plane->quad is 571 at N=60k and 31 at N=534, against a penalty of 6. Cup cone->poly4 is 795 against a penalty of 6. With eps fixed at 2 mm, the decision depends on voxel size (board ep23: cubic at 1-2 mm, plane at 4 and 8 mm). Our stereo points are spatially correlated, so the per-point penalty is not calibrated and the outcome depends on how densely we sample. [H] It could work with an effective sample size, e.g. one sample per correlation length or per frame, but that size is itself a tuning knob. Falsify: if no single N_eff gives plane for both boards and lathe for both cups without object-specific tuning, drop the 'adopt'. The lathe gate is also a non-nested family question (revolution or not), outside the nested degeneracy setting the paper's experiments address.

checked.claim: Slippage analysis (verdict test): Gelfand and Guibas SGP 2004 on scanned mechanical parts; Schnabel 2007 calls it costly and 'sensitive to noise'; classes are plane, sphere, cylinder, surface of revolution, helix, extrusion; needs large segments on noisy normals [E]
checked.how_checked: Abstract via web search (DOI 10.2312/SGP/SGP04/219-228). The Stanford PDF gave connection resets and 503, and diglib returned 403. Schnabel quote checked in s07.txt (line 189). [M] Slippage spectra (6x6, normalised eigenvalues) from the same probe at 2 mm voxels.
checked.correction: The abstract confirms scanned mechanical parts and reverse engineering. Schnabel's exact words are 'costly for large models, the method is sensitive to noise and it is hard to determine the correct size of the initial surface patches'. The helix class could not be seen directly. [M] On pre-segmented regions the spectrum is clear. Board face: [0.018, 0.018, 0.022, 0.24, ...], 3 slippable motions, so plane. Cup outer wall: [0.047, 0.063, 0.38, ...], 2, so cylinder. On whole clouds there is no clean gap. Cup [0.16, 0.26, 0.36], lid [0.17, 0.25, 0.27], pitcher [0.30, 0.38, 0.39]; the pot [0.25, 0.57] shows only a weak single-rotation signal. So it needs a segmentation front end. My segments came from fitted models, so seed-grown local patches (the paper's actual method) remain untested.

missed_methods: CGAL Python bindings (pip 'cgal' 6.0.1, GPL): efficient_RANSAC including tori, plus plane region growing. This lets the RANSAC 'test' run the reference implementation on CPU instead of a numpy reimplementation without tori [M: read binding source].

Variational Shape Approximation (Cohen-Steiner, Alliez, Desbrun 2004) and hybrid VSA with planes, spheres, cylinders and rolling-ball blends (Wu and Kobbelt, Eurographics 2005): proxy partitions that automatically trade proxy count against an error budget [L, not re-checked].
Hierarchical fitting primitives (Attene, Falcidieno, Spagnuolo 2006; Attene and Patane 2010 for point sets): automatic bottom-up clustering by plane, sphere and cylinder fit cost [L, not re-checked].

Classical reverse-engineering B-rep pipelines (Varady, Martin, Cox 1997; Benko and Varady 2004): automatic detection of translational and rotational sweeps and fillets on engineered parts. The closest classical analogue of an automated kit-of-parts [L, not re-checked].
J-Linkage / T-Linkage (Toldo and Fusiello 2008; Magri and Fusiello 2014): multi-model fitting without a known model count, with code. Only mentioned in the report as a comparison [L].
GoCoPP (Yu and Lafarge, CVPR 2022): planar-primitive configurations with an MDL-like energy; candidate for boards and dust-pan faces [L].

Generalized Cylinder Decomposition (Zhou et al., SIGGRAPH Asia 2015) and ROSA rotational-symmetry-axis skeletons from incomplete point clouds (Tagliasacchi et al. 2009): automatic handle, sweeper and spoon parts. The L1-medial skeleton is already in lit/primitives-cad.md [L].

Symmetry detection as the automatic family selector (Mitra, Guibas, Pauly 2006; Podolak et al. 2006; Thrun and Wegbreit 2005): continuous rotation means lathe, a mirror plane means plate or extrusion. Covered in lit/primitives-cad.md section 3 but absent from this report.

Visibility / free-space consistency as a selector term (Curless and Levoy 1996 space carving; Laurentini 1994 visual hull), using the 'free' and 'hits' grids already stored in our obs npz files: penalises candidate surface in observed-empty space. A GT-free complement to obs_fidelity [H]. Falsify: Spearman vs CD-O on the 32 pot candidates does not rise above 0.85.

Hough-transform cylinder detection (Rabbani and van den Heuvel 2005) and Gaussian-image axis estimation (Chaperon and Goulette 2001): deterministic axis and cylinder proposals as alternatives to RANSAC [L].

Correlated-error model selection: BIC or MDL with an effective sample size, or GRIC as already cited. This is needed before any G-AIC-style criterion can be used on dense stereo points (see the refutation above).
verification.summary:
Most literature, licence and number claims in the classic-methods report check out against primary sources. One 'adopt' verdict does not survive our data, and the report missed a ready-made library.

Refuted [M]: the 'adopt' for geometric AIC/MDL as a way to replace hand thresholds. A new GT-free probe (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/90d4009c-b597-536b-9d55-58f81afca135/scratchpad/verify_probe/gaic_slip_probe.py, output run1.jsonl in the same folder; reads only obs pts/cam) fitted boards and blue-cup walls at 1-8 mm voxels. G-AIC always picks the most flexible model, even for RMS gains of 0.01-0.03 mm. Its fit-gain-to-penalty ratio grows with the point count (571 vs a penalty of 6 at 60k points), and with a fixed sigma the decision flips with voxel size. Our stereo points are spatially correlated, so the per-point penalty is not calibrated. It needs an effective sample size [H], which is itself a tuning knob.

Supported with caveats:
- Recover-and-select as the automation principle: grow over-complete part hypotheses, then select. The method is confirmed from the abstracts. The ECCV 1994 authors are Leonardis, Solina and Macerl, and the MDL label and 'real range images' for the 1995 paper could not be verified.
- Slippage as an automatic family test [M]: clean plane and cylinder signatures on segmented regions (board face, cup outer wall), no clean signature on whole clouds. It therefore needs a segmentation front end; seed-grown patches are untested.
- Efficient RANSAC: the quotes, Table 1 timings and research-only licence are confirmed, but the cited ArmarX URL is dead (the ReadMe is in the CloudCompare repo). The [M] probe numbers match the logs, but the reimplementation has no tori, so the handle claim is [E]. Loosening it turns the pot body into large spheres.
- The report missed that pip 'cgal' 6.0.1 exposes efficient_RANSAC with tori in Python, so the reference implementation can be tested on CPU.

Minor corrections: GlobFit's archive declares GPL-3, not only 'research use'. Multi-X is on GitHub (danini/multi-x, no licence file). CGAL sphere and cylinder region growing predates 6.x. All arXiv IDs exist.

No scans, alignment files, mocap or poses were read. No repo edits.

methods.name: openshape3d scan_to_cad (Laan Labs): revolve-first, then a recursive residual fit of sweeps, revolves and extrudes
methods.source: GitHub repo laanlabs/openshape3d, docs/SCAN_TO_CAD.md and PR #116
methods.code_url: https://github.com/laanlabs/openshape3d (scripts/scan_to_cad/: analyze_scan.py, fit_axes.py, fit_features.py, fit_primitives.py, inspect_fit.py)
methods.cpu_feasible: Yes [L]. The fitting is numpy/trimesh/scipy. Only the B-rep build goes through the iPad/Mac app over MCP (OCCT); a manifold3d union could replace that step for us [E].
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: Yes [L]. One recipe ran on 11 real Sketchfab phone or handheld scans with missing undersides: hydrants, extinguishers, a bollard, a pail, a tin barrel, a WD40 can, a beer mug, a wheel, a valve. Beer mug after the 25 Oct rebuild: overlap 97 %, model→scan 1.4 mm, scan→model 0.8 mm mean, handle partly missing (WARN). Hydrant (858 mm): mean 12.1 / 8.1 mm. Oval or dented scans FAIL. Caveat: per-part overrides live in analysis-flags.json (--flip, --units, --band, --axis), so it is not fully hands-off [L].
methods.output: Valid B-rep solid (STL/STEP/OBJ): revolve bodies on one or more axes, with cavities (solid revolve minus a wall offset) plus swept tubes, cones and extruded plates. Two-way inspection gates on the largest missing or excess patch.
methods.fit_to_our_problem: The closest automated precedent for our cups, pot, lid and pitcher plus handles, and it is classical, not learned. It splits the residual into pieces and tries sweep, revolve and extrude on each, keeping the best coverage with bonuses for simple shapes (recursion depth 3). It also has a library of named parts (stadium, rounded rectangle, hexagon, hoop). The input is a complete mesh, not partial stereo points, and it has no rack, sheet (dust pan) or thin-board families.
methods.reported_accuracy: Self-reported mean surface deviations 0.2–9 mm on real scans, and 1.0 mm on its synthetic stand-in with 0.7 mm noise [L]. No standard benchmark.

methods.name: CADENA (stepwise CAD reverse engineering)
methods.licence: Code MIT, weights MIT [M: LICENSE plus the HF API card]. The base is Qwen2-VL.
methods.cpu_feasible: Not as shipped: the README says serving the policy needs an NVIDIA GPU (vLLM). The DSL runtime and metrics run on CPU [L]. Greedy decoding takes up to 20 steps; beam search draws 12 candidates per step.
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: None. It is evaluated only on DeepCAD, Fusion360, MCB, CADENA-Bench and BenchCAD (synthetic CAD) [L]. It keeps a step only if IoU against the target mesh improves, so it needs a closed target mesh [L: README].
methods.output: A CadQuery-based DSL program built one operation at a time; ops include extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, shell, chamfer, fillet and gear [L].
methods.fit_to_our_problem: The only learned program model found with revolve, sweep and shell and permissive weights. Its input is renders of a complete mesh, and it was trained on procedurally generated mechanical parts. Feeding it our TSDF would reproduce the thick walls; feeding it splats of our partial points is untested [H]. At best it proposes structure, and the numbers must be refit to our points.
methods.weights_or_training: SFT on 1.86 M + 18.0 M procedurally generated programs, then RL on about 4k MCB/DeepCAD/Fusion360 meshes [L]
methods.reported_accuracy: Greedy IoU: DeepCAD 96.1, Fusion360 94.1, MCB 88.2, against CAD-Recode 91.4 / 87.2 / 71.1 [L]

methods.name: CAD-Recode (v1, v1.5)
methods.licence: CC BY-NC 4.0 for the repo (LICENSE.md) and the v1 and v1.5 HF weights [M]. This corrects the earlier lit note, which said the licence had not been read.
methods.cpu_feasible: Possible in principle: Qwen2-1.5B plus a point projector, 10 sampled candidates [L]. About 1.8 s per sample on an H100 [L, cadrille Table 9]; on our 4-core CPU, minutes per candidate [E].
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: CC3D: 2,973 real Artec scans of mechanical CAD parts, with noise, smoothed edges and missing parts. v1.5 scores mean CD 0.765, median CD 0.313 (×10³), IoU 74.2 %, invalid 0.3 % [L: CHANGELOG]. CD is the sum of the two directional mean squared distances in a unit box [M: cadrille evaluate.py read]. That is ≈1.2 % (median) to ≈2 % (mean) of box size as RMS per direction [E].
methods.output: CadQuery Python, which runs to a B-rep or mesh
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Poor. The training corpus is circles and rectangles extruded on 3 canonical planes, with union and cut. It has no revolve, sweep, fillet or shell; the authors name revolve and B-splines as failure sources [L]. So it cannot express thin hollow revolved walls, handles or spouts.

key_insights: Direct answer to 'are they case by case?' Partly. The fitting and the selection are automatic: every number comes from our stereo points, and obs_fidelity picks the candidate without GT. The template is per object type: which parts exist, and which family each part uses. Agents wrote those templates per object name (prim_potlid.py, prim_rack.py, prim_boards.py, lathe_obs.py). The pot 0.437→0.342, lid 0.421→0.220 and rack 0.555→0.456 gains [D] come from those hand-designed templates.

No learned model found (2018 to Oct 2026) builds part structure automatically for our household objects at the accuracy we need on real, partial, noisy data [L]. The learned CAD-code models (CAD-Recode, cadrille, CADReasoner, CADonatello, CAD-SIGNet, TransCAD, DeepCAD) are trained on sketch-extrude mechanical parts. CAD-Recode's corpus has no revolve, sweep, fillet or shell, and its authors name revolve as a failure source [L]. So these models cannot express thin hollow revolved walls with handles: cups, pot, lid, pitcher.

The only real-scan benchmark is CC3D: mechanical parts scanned by Artec, complete closed shapes. CAD-Recode v1.5 scores median CD 0.313e-3, mean 0.765e-3, IoU 74.2 % [L]; cadrille-RL 0.47e-3 / 67.9 % [L]; CADonatello 0.48e-3 [L]. I read cadrille's evaluate.py: CD is the sum of the two directional mean squared distances in a unit box [M]. So the median is about 1.2 % and the mean about 2 % of box size as RMS distance [E]. That is on in-family mechanical shapes. Our leaders sit near 1 %, our lathe near 2.4 %.

Learned primitive segmentation fails on real depth. View2CAD reports that Point2CAD with HPNet segmentation over-segmented a real RealSense scan, so B-rep extraction failed, and Split-and-Fit produced nothing [L]. BPNet shows only 4 qualitative real scans [L]. SPFN, ParSeNet, HPNet and PrimitiveNet are trained on ABC or TraceParts and need clean normals.

Generic primitive abstraction stays at about 2–4 % of size: SuperDec L1 1.70e-2 on ScanNet++, SuperFlex 3.98e-2 on partial ASE, PrimitiveAnything CD 0.040 on a unit cube with 85 % cuboids [L]. CSG nets (CSGNet, UCSG-Net, CSG-Stump, CAPRI-Net, D²CSG, ExtrudeNet, SECAD-Net) and convex or part nets (CvxNet, BSP-Net, Neural Parts) are ShapeNet/ABC voxel abstractions, and several need per-shape GPU fine-tuning [L]. None is useful as a final mesh. At most they could model blob parts.

Licence corrections versus the 26 Oct lit note [M]: CAD-Recode repo and weights are CC BY-NC 4.0. cadrille code is Apache-2.0 but its weights are CC BY-NC 4.0. MeshCoder code is MIT but its weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and gated. PrimitiveAnything is GPL-3.0. PartField is NVIDIA non-commercial. Hunyuan3D-Part (P3-SAM) excludes the EU, UK and South Korea. Permissive weights: CADReasoner (Apache-2.0) and CADENA (MIT). No LICENSE file found: ParSeNet, HPNet, CSGNet, D²CSG, GeoCode, BPNet.

All learned program models expect a complete closed target normalised to a unit box: points sampled from a closed mesh, or renders of one. CADENA keeps a step only when IoU against the target improves [L]. Our input is partial: no undersides, interiors partly unseen, double thin walls. Given our TSDF as the target, they would reproduce its thick walls; given only our points, their behaviour is untested [H].

CADENA (Aug 2026) is the only learned program model found with revolve, sweep, loft and shell plus permissive (MIT) weights [L, M]. But it is trained only on procedurally generated mechanical parts, evaluated only on synthetic CAD, and needs an NVIDIA GPU (vLLM) [L]. MeshCoder is the only one whose training categories include Cup and Spoon, and it has arrays for the rack, but it is synthetic-only with NC-SA weights [L]. Either could at most propose structure, with the numbers refit by our optimisers.

The best automated precedent is classical and permissively licensed: openshape3d scan_to_cad (MIT, Oct 2026) [L]. One recipe finds every revolve axis, traces the profile and makes containers as a solid revolve minus a wall offset. It splits the residual into pieces and tries sweep, revolve and extrude on each, keeping the best coverage with simplicity bonuses (recursion depth 3). A library of named parts (stadium, rounded rectangle, hexagon, hoop, one-spine tube) regularises the pieces. A two-way inspection gates on the largest missing or excess patch. Real beer-mug scan: about 1.1–1.4 mm model→scan and 0.7–0.8 mm scan→model mean [L]. It still uses per-part flags, and its inputs are complete phone-scan meshes.

The same 'automated kit-of-parts' architecture appears in the papers. Point2CAD fits every type to every cluster and keeps the lowest residual. CADonatello runs a foundation segmenter and then a fitter per part. View2CAD runs RANSAC, then a global LM with shared axes. So the automated route is a generic dispatcher: a small family library, residual-driven segmentation, per-family fitters, and GT-free selection with a complexity penalty. Our existing scripts already contain most of the families: closed-profile lathe, bar or sweep handle, extruded outline, peg array, marker balls.

[H] One generic dispatcher with no code branching on object names would match the hand-specialised fitters. Families: thin-wall SOR shell; residual sweep tube; residual plate or extrude; 1-D array of a repeated part; superquadric blob; marker balls. Selection: obs_fidelity plus a coverage term and a BIC/MDL-style part-count penalty, which also counters the known thin-sheet bias. Falsifying test (a pre-registered public-episode round, diagnostic scoring once): it fails if any of pot, lid, blue cup or rack scores more than 0.03 cm worse in CD-O than its hand fitter, or flips more often.

Expected limits of a generic dispatcher [E]: the rack (28 % coverage, fins hide each other) and the boards (identity-safe tracks, slots) still need priors or tracking fixes, not just more families. The spoon, the sweeper handle and the dust-pan scoop need two families our scripts lack: a generalized-cylinder sweep whose cross-section varies, and a shelled sheet.

Cost: every adopt or test path that is classical runs on our 4-core CPU at $0 [E]. Every learned CAD-code model needs a GPU as shipped (vLLM, CUDA ops, xformers) [L], and so needs an owner-approved rental. Running third-party weights was out of scope for this workflow, so I measured nothing on our data here [M: no runs].
top_claims_to_verify: CAD-Recode's training corpus, which cadrille and CADReasoner reuse, has only sketch-extrude with union and cut: no revolve, sweep, fillet or shell. So these models structurally cannot represent our thin-walled revolved cups, pot, lid and pitcher. Check §3 of https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14042 and sample programs in https://huggingface.co/datasets/filapro/cad-recode-v1.5.

No learned primitive or CAD model has published accuracy at or below about 1 % of object size on real, partial, noisy scans of household objects. The strongest real-scan evidence is CC3D (mechanical parts, complete scans): CAD-Recode v1.5 median CD 0.313e-3, which converts to about 1.2 % (median) and 2 % (mean) RMS of box size under cadrille's evaluate.py formula (sum of mean squared distances, unit box). Check the formula in https://github.com/col14m/cadrille/blob/master/evaluate.py and the CC3D normalisation.

Weights licences: CAD-Recode (v1, v1.5) and cadrille (SFT, RL) are CC BY-NC 4.0. MeshCoder is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and gated. PrimitiveAnything is GPL-3.0. CADENA (MIT) and CADReasoner (Apache-2.0) are permissive. Check the HF model cards (filapro/cad-recode-v1.5, maksimko123/cadrille-rl, InternRobotics/MeshCoder, kulibinai/cadena) and whether the V2D rules allow non-commercial weights in a submission.

Learned primitive segmentation trained on ABC does not transfer to real depth: View2CAD reports that Point2CAD with HPNet segmentation over-segmented a real RealSense scan, and B-rep extraction failed. Check the real-data comparison section and figures of https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.04000.

A generic classical recipe can rebuild real scanned household objects at about 1 mm mean deviation: openshape3d scan_to_cad reports beer mug model→scan 1.1–1.4 mm and scan→model 0.7–0.8 mm. Check the tables in https://github.com/laanlabs/openshape3d/blob/main/docs/SCAN_TO_CAD.md, and how much depends on the per-part overrides in corpus/analysis-flags.json (--flip, --units, --band, --axis). Those overrides decide whether it is really automatic.
open_questions: Do the V2D Track 3 rules allow non-commercial (CC BY-NC / NC-SA) or GPL model weights, or third-party structure proposals, in a submitted method? This decides whether CAD-Recode, cadrille or MeshCoder are even candidates; CADENA and CADReasoner avoid the issue.

Would a generic, name-agnostic dispatcher (one family library plus residual segmentation plus GT-free selection) match the hand-specialised fitters on pot, lid, blue cup and rack? This needs a pre-registered public-episode round, with diagnostic scoring done once.

Can obs_fidelity choose between families of different complexity without its thin-sheet bias? What penalty (BIC/MDL on the part count, an area prior from the observed silhouette, a coverage term) keeps its Spearman with CD-O near 0.85 across families, not only within one family?

What families do the spoon, sweeper and dust pan need? Candidates: a generalized-cylinder sweep with varying cross-section (spoon handle, sweeper handle), a shelled sheet (dust pan), a superquadric block (bristles). Our points cannot see the dust-pan underside or the spoon bowl's back, so how is the thickness set without GT?

Can CADENA or MeshCoder take renders or splats of PARTIAL stereo points, not a closed mesh? Would their structure proposals ever beat our classical residual segmentation? This needs a GPU probe on public objects only, with the owner's go-ahead and an expected cost of a few dollars.
For the pitcher, are a spout displacement field and a swept handle enough for the generic dispatcher, or does it need a multi-axis SOR like openshape3d's fit_axes?

How does any family fit behave at eval time? The eval meshes are built from public-episode points, since there is no eval depth cache, so per-episode fitting cannot use eval observations until eval depth exists.

missed_methods: CADFit (Nehme, Whalen, Ahmed; ICML 2026; arXiv 2605.01171; github.com/ghadinehme/CADFit). Optimises volumetric IoU over executable CadQuery programs with Extrude, Revolve, Fillet, Chamfer, Union and Cut, and refits positive and negative residuals with union/cut until the residual volume is small. It is the closest academic counterpart to openshape3d's residual loop. Its requirements are CPU-only (cadquery, manifold3d, trimesh, pymeshlab, scipy); a DINOv2 sketch filter is optional. It needs a watertight mesh. Licence CC BY-NC 4.0, with a provisional patent filed [L: README, LICENSE and requirements read]. In CADENA's Table 1 it is the strongest baseline on MCB IoU (75.8), but 25-30 % of parts do not converge within budget [L].

CADEvolve (arXiv 2602.16317; github.com/zhemdi/CADEvolve; HF kulibinai/cadevolve-rl1; Apache-2.0 code and weights). A VLM trained on 1.3 M evolved CadQuery scripts covering revolve, loft, sweep, shell, fillet and chamfer; image input [L]. It contradicts the report's claim that CADENA is the only permissive model with revolve, sweep and shell.

P3-SAM (Tencent Hunyuan3D-Part, arXiv 2509.06784). The 3-D part segmenter CADONATELLO uses as its front end; it is the natural first stage of an automated kit-of-parts pipeline (segment, then fit each part). Licence: Tencent Hunyuan 3D-Part Community Licence, which excludes the EU, UK and South Korea [L: LICENSE header read].

PartField (NVIDIA, ICCV 2025, github.com/nv-tlabs/PartField). Feed-forward 3-D part feature fields with hierarchical clustering, an alternative part segmenter. NVIDIA licence, likely non-commercial [L: LICENSE header read; terms not fully read].
StepCAD (NeurIPS 2026): mesh-to-CAD code generation with an LLM policy plus geometry-guided search [L: search result only; unverified].

Further learned CAD-program work cited in CADENA and not covered: SOV-CAD (Feng et al. 2026, iterative visual feedback, offline RL), CADFS (Pyatov et al. 2026, FeatureScript with 15 operations), Zero-to-CAD (Ataei et al. 2026), Pointer-CAD (Qi et al. 2026, B-rep pointers for fillet and chamfer), IterCAD (Hu et al. 2026) [L: CADENA related work; unverified].

BenchCAD Vision2Code board (as reported in CADENA Table 3): frontier VLMs writing CadQuery reach voxel IoU of at most 0.706 (GPT-5.6) and 0.355 after regrading, while CADENA reaches 0.910 [L]. This is evidence that a general LLM writing programs directly is weak, whereas LLM-written fitters plus numeric refits (our current approach) remain untested in the literature.
verification.summary:
I checked every 'adopt' and 'test' method and most reference entries against primary sources: GitHub raw files, the arXiv API and HTML, the HF model API, and the official CC3D page. I did not run anything, did not read any scans, ground truth or weights, and did not edit the repo.

openshape3d ('adopt') is real, MIT-licensed and well described. Of all the methods in the report, it is the only one with numbers on real physical scans with missing regions [L]. The verdict overstates how directly it can be used:
- **App dependency:** the revolve body and its export are built in the OpenShape 3D iPad/Mac app (DEBUG build in an Xcode simulator), and fit_features.py takes that export as its --model input. The chain therefore does not run on our Linux CPU VM without our own builder; the manifold3d substitute is only an estimate [E].
- **Input:** it needs a triangle mesh (face adjacency), not a point cloud.
- **Beer mug:** the inspection verdict is FAIL, not WARN.
- **Bonuses:** the +0.08 / +0.05 bonuses favour sweep and revolve; they are not simplicity bonuses.
- **Plates:** plate and flange parts exist, but only as attachments to a revolve body.
- **Manual flags:** per-part flags are needed.

So it supports 'automated within a family (turned bodies plus attachments)', not 'hands-off'. The right move is to adopt the design pattern (revolve first, residual pieces, two-way largest-patch gate) and port it to our points, not the code.

CADENA ('test'): licence (MIT code and weights), GPU need, operations, IoU numbers and training sizes all check out. Two corrections:
- MCB and CADENA-Bench are real industrial CAD parts, not synthetic, but still mechanical parts and not scans.
- It is not the only permissive model with revolve, sweep and shell: CADEvolve has Apache-2.0 code and weights with the same operation set.

A test also conflicts with this workflow's no-third-party-weights rule. It needs a GPU, or unmeasured slow CPU inference through transformers [E]. It also needs a watertight target, and our only watertight targets are the thick-walled TSDF meshes.

Three decision-relevant factual errors elsewhere:
1. CC3D is not real Artec scans. The official page says the CAD meshes were virtually scanned with Artec3D's proprietary pipeline. No learned CAD-program method in the report has quantitative results on real physical scans.
2. CADReasoner does evaluate on CC3D: v2 supplementary Table 7 gives CC3D-scan CD 0.37 and IoU 66.7.
3. MeshCoder's categories include Lid, Bowl, Jar, Vase and Bottle as well as Cup and Spoon, so it covers more of our objects than the report says. MegaParts is a text- and box-conditioned generator, not a MeshCoder follow-up.

All the licence findings for the rejected repos held up.

Important omissions:
- **CADFit** (ICML 2026): CPU dependencies, extrude/revolve/fillet/chamfer with residual union/cut. It is the closest academic counterpart to openshape3d's residual loop, but it is CC BY-NC with a patent filed and needs a watertight mesh.
- **CADEvolve**: see above.
- **P3-SAM and PartField**: part-segmenter front ends, both under restrictive licences.

Hypothesis [H]: an openshape3d-style residual fitter ported to our observed points, with our selector, beats our hand-designed per-object fitters on the objects where it applies (lathe-type bodies: cups, pot, lid, pitcher). Falsifying test: run it unchanged on all objects in a pre-registered round and score with obs_fidelity and CD-O. It fails if it does not match prim_potlid and lathe_obs (pot 0.342, lid 0.220, blue cup 0.291 [D]) on those objects.

methods.name: [H] In-house proposal: fixed part DSL + residual-driven assembly + deterministic optimiser + GT-free selection (no LLM at run time)
methods.source: This review, built from our scripts (lathe_obs.py, prim_potlid.py, prim_rack.py, prim_boards.py) and from section 2.5 of lit/primitives-cad.md (Efficient RANSAC, GC decomposition with MDL)
methods.cpu_feasible: Yes [M]: lid fit 3.4-4.4 s, pot fit about 75 s, obs_fidelity 3.3 s per candidate on this 4-core VM
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: Yes, by construction: it uses our own stereo points
methods.output: A per-object recipe (root body type + allowed part types + priors) chosen from the object name or by enumeration. The root body is fitted first; residual clusters are tried against every part type; a part is kept only if it improves fidelity beyond an MDL/BIC penalty. Optionally an LLM proposes K recipes offline, and they are frozen in git
methods.fit_to_our_problem: Turns case-by-case authoring into a reproducible search. The literature says this split works best (structure discrete, numbers by optimiser, selection by fit to the input). Falsifying test (pre-registered, later round): re-derive pot, lid and rack with the generic pipeline and no per-object code. If the GT-free fidelity of the selected meshes is worse than the hand-authored ones by more than 10%, or (scoring round) CD-O is worse than 0.342 / 0.220 / 0.456, the hypothesis is falsified.

key_insights: Direct answer to the owner [M]: yes, the authoring is case by case today; only fitting and selection are automatic. Each family fitter was hand-written by an agent: prim_potlid.py 836 lines with 18 module-level constants, prim_rack.py 884 / 19, prim_boards.py 681 / 12, lathe_obs.py 323 / 3. Once written, the fitters are fully reproducible: two runs each of the lid (ep2) and pot (ep41) fitters gave bit-identical GLBs (sha256 0bac47f4... and 355ad72e...). Lid takes 3.4-4.4 s, pot about 75 s, and obs_fidelity 3.3 s per candidate on this CPU VM (commit 704162c).

[L] No published system does the full loop we want (an LLM or VLM writes a part program from images and points, an optimiser fits it, and a GT-free reward selects it) on REAL partial noisy scans at about 1% accuracy. Real-scan evidence is limited to CC3D mechanical parts (CAD-Recode, cadrille) and qualitative demos (CAD-Assistant, Articulate-Anything). Infinigen, PartNet, DeepCAD, CADPrompt, BlenderGym and 3DCodeBench are synthetic.

[L] The consistent finding: LLMs and VLMs are reasonable at choosing structure and poor at metric numbers. BlenderGym geometry CD: human 0.334 vs best VLM 1.120. 3D-PreMise: GPT-4 pass@1 7-17.5%, with spatial-precision errors the most common. ParSEL: LLMs find the first operation but rarely a complete program. autoresearch HPO: CMA-ES and TPE consistently beat LLM agents on continuous parameters. So in any automated version the LLM proposes parts and topology, and least_squares, CMA-ES or our medians fit every number.

[L] Visual VLM self-critique is a weak reward; geometric feedback is strong. CADCodeVerify: VLM-question feedback 0.153 -> 0.132 point-cloud distance vs 0.102 for geometric feedback (which uses GT); no gain beyond 2 refinements; the VLM answered its own checks correctly 64.6% of the time. Query2CAD saturates at the 2nd refinement (76.7%). The Articulate-Anything critic adds +2.4 to +5.8% and gives false positives. BlenderGym's best VLM verifier agrees with humans 0.66 vs 0.79 human-human. 3DHarnessBench: adding explicit geometric measurements cuts Chamfer 0.0150 -> 0.0084, and full measurement access gives 0.002-0.003 vs 0.011-0.016 multi-view. Our obs_fidelity is a geometric reward of this kind; keep it as the primary signal and use a VLM only for coarse structure checks such as 'is there a handle'.

[L] Best-of-N with a GT-free fit-to-input selector is the best-supported automation step on real scans. CAD-Recode on CC3D with 10 candidates kept by minimum Chamfer to the input: CD 3.05 -> 0.76, invalid 16.8% -> 0.3%. StepCAD and BlenderAlchemy add local search around the current best, with reversion. Our verification is cheap (3.3 s [M]), so the budget should go to many structural candidates, not to long refinement chains (BlenderGym: as compute grows, a larger share should go to verification).

[L] Execution-error retries fix crashes, not geometry. 3DCodeBench: the agent harness lifts executability 0.716 -> 0.995 while shape metrics barely change. Query2CAD: 69% of GPT-4T failures were code that would not run. A fixed typed DSL (parts with bounded parameters, as in Embodied CAD's skill library, AIDL and ReliCAD's deterministic kernel) removes most of that failure class by construction.

[L] Reproducibility: hosted LLMs are not deterministic even at temperature 0 (80 unique completions out of 1000, Thinking Machines 2025). An automated authoring pipeline must therefore freeze the LLM's outputs: commit the prompt, model id, raw responses and the generated recipe or code, and treat them as source. Everything after that (our fitters and selector) is deterministic [M]. This also satisfies the CLAUDE.md rule to commit the exact code of every submitted run.

[L] Single LLM calls vary a lot, so more than one proposal is needed. ShapeLib makes 5 proposals per seed and 4 implementations per function, validates each by executing it against seed shapes, and found 5-10% of proposals buggy; validated library F-score 54.0 vs LLM-only 37.4. For us 'seed validation' is: the proposed part program must improve obs_fidelity on the public episodes of that object.

[H] A no-LLM automatic route probably captures most of the value: a fixed part DSL plus residual-driven assembly (fit the root body, cluster residuals, try every part type, accept a part only if the fidelity gain beats an MDL/BIC penalty). The parts already exist in our scripts: closed-profile lathe, bar handle, swept arch strap, extruded outline, rounded-rect tray minus basin, peg rows, marker sphere plus stem. The object name picks the root type. Falsify: on public episodes, the generic pipeline's selected meshes must match the hand-authored pot, lid and rack fidelity within 10%, and later CD-O (pre-registered round).

[M] Reward bias, GT-free probe (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/90d4009c-b597-536b-9d55-58f81afca135/scratchpad/probe_scripts/vis_probe.py). The obs_points npz files already store 4 mm hits/free voxel grids. Share of fitted mesh area in voxels our cameras saw through ('carved'): pot fit 0.068, pot thick 0.177, lid 0.022. Share in never-observed voxels: 3.2-7.5%. Mesh-to-obs distance there is 3.7-5.6 mm vs 0.7-1.0 mm on seen area. obs_fidelity's bounding-box mesh_to_obs term penalises that unobserved area, which is the thin-sheet bias. [H] A visibility-aware reward (penalise carved surface, ignore unobserved) would remove the bias. Falsify in a pre-registered round: its Spearman vs the existing CD-O of the 32 pot candidates must exceed 0.85. Caveat: 4 mm voxels cannot separate a 3 mm floor from its underside.

[I] Integrity benefit: automating authoring with a fixed prompt and logged inputs (crops, our points, object name; never scans) structurally prevents the leak found in the lid and rack round, where scan-measured thicknesses reached the builders through a brief. Every prompt and input becomes auditable.

[L] Licences: CAD-Recode code CC BY-NC 4.0, CAD-Assistant CC BY-NC 4.0, Text2CAD CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, ShapeAssembly Brown non-commercial-product clause. MeshCoder MIT and cadrille Apache-2.0 [M: LICENSE files fetched]. CADCodeVerify, Query2CAD and BlenderAlchemyOfficial have no root LICENSE file. Reuse ideas, not code. All weight-based models are excluded this round anyway.

[E] Cost: an agentic full-interaction authoring run costs about 4.5-7.9 per object in 3DHarnessBench (units unstated, likely USD) with 18-51 tool calls. For 11 objects x 3-5 structural proposals that is about $50-400 [E], against $0 for the deterministic DSL route. CAD-Assistant reports $0.03-0.09 per request.
top_claims_to_verify: CAD-Recode, Table 3 (https://arxiv.org/html/2412.14042): on real CC3D scans, sampling 10 candidates and keeping the one with minimum Chamfer to the INPUT point cloud lowers CD 3.05 -> 0.76 and the invalid rate 16.8% -> 0.3%. If true, GT-free fit-to-input selection over many structures is the right automation core.

CADCodeVerify, Table 2 and Appendix B.3 (https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05340v2): VLM-question feedback improves GPT-4 point-cloud distance only 0.153 -> 0.132, while GT geometric-solver feedback reaches 0.102. There is no gain beyond 2 refinements, and the VLM answers its own checks correctly only 64.6% of the time. If true, the reward should be geometric (our points), not a VLM judge.

3DHarnessBench, Tables 1 and 10 (https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06535): frontier agents with Blender-MCP measurement access reach Chamfer 0.002-0.003 vs 0.011-0.016 multi-view, and measurements alone cut 0.0150 -> 0.0084. Check whether the 'Full 3D Interaction' agent effectively queries the true complete target. If so, the gain overstates what an agent gets from our partial noisy points.

3DCodeBench (https://arxiv.org/html/2606.01057): the coding-agent harness raises executability 0.716 -> 0.995 while conditional shape metrics barely change. If true, execution feedback buys robustness, not accuracy, and a typed DSL makes it largely unnecessary.

Ferreira et al. 2026 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24647): CMA-ES and TPE consistently beat LLM agents at tuning a fixed continuous search space, and a CMA-ES+LLM hybrid is best. If true, the LLM should never set numeric part parameters directly.
open_questions: Is a single fixed part DSL expressive enough for the objects without a fitter yet (mini_sweeper, mini_dust_pan, water_pitcher spout, wooden_spoon with no public scan), or does each still need a new part type? That would mean case-by-case authoring again, but of parts rather than whole objects.

Does obs_fidelity's Spearman 0.85 (measured on 32 parametric pot variants) hold across STRUCTURAL alternatives (handle present or absent, lathe vs sheet vs extrusion)? Structure selection is exactly where an automated pipeline relies on it. This needs a pre-registered scoring round.

Can a silhouette term be computed GT-free? It needs per-frame object masks and camera-from-object poses from our own tracks. The obs npz has camera centres and frame ids but no masks; I have not checked whether the pipeline keeps SAM2 masks.

A finer visibility grid: the 4 mm hits/free grid cannot separate a 2-4 mm wall's inner and outer faces. Would re-running obs_points.py with vox about 1.5 mm, or per-frame ray casting, make a visibility-aware reward usable for thin walls?

Should an LLM be called at all at pipeline run time? It makes runs non-reproducible and costs money. The alternative: an LLM or agent proposes recipes offline once per object, they are frozen and committed, and an owner decides on API spend.
The board failures (flip on 1 of 6 seeds; the ep23 board-2 track looks like board 1) are track-identity and registration problems. Automating mesh authoring will not fix them. Who owns that fix?
Do the organisers consider an LLM-authored part program fitted only to our observations 'own reconstruction'? I expect yes (no third-party geometry), but this is unconfirmed.

verification.summary:
I checked the report's two 'test' verdicts and most of its decision-relevant numbers against the primary sources (arXiv HTML, repo LICENSE and README files, Hugging Face model pages). Most numbers are quoted correctly [L]. The interpretations need these corrections:

**ShapeLib**
- Its '37.4 vs 54.0 with validation' comparison is not a validation ablation. LLM-only skips the seed set entirely.
- Its acceptance test is coarse: matched-primitive distance <=0.25 on unit-sphere shapes, with clean, complete, part-segmented PartNet seeds.
- So it shows that 'many proposals plus executable validation' works at category level. It gives no evidence on mm-level fitting to partial noisy points.

**3DHarnessBench**
- The 0.002 Chamfer under Full 3D comes from an agent allowed to measure the ground-truth mesh exactly (bounding boxes, distances, symmetry planes).
- The measurement ablation (0.0150 -> 0.0084) is 10 instances, one model, one run, with no variance reported.
- Cost figures cover 3 models and have no stated currency. MCP calls run 18-67, not 18-51.

**CAD-Recode**
- The authors say test-time sampling 'mainly helps reducing' the invalid-output rate, and they do not say how invalid outputs enter CD.
- So 3.05 -> 0.76 is weaker evidence for choosing between valid structures by fit to the input than the report claims.

**CADCodeVerify**
- The 64.6% includes 'Unclear' answers. On Yes/No answers the VLM is 87-91% correct.
- Its headline 0.132 is an undefined 'Best Refine' value below both per-step medians, likely per-example oracle selection [inference].

**Licences and weights (confirmed)**
- CAD-Recode CC BY-NC 4.0 with HF weights; cadrille Apache-2.0 with HF weights; MeshCoder MIT, NeurIPS 2025, with an object-to-code checkpoint now on HF.
- Text2CAD CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; CAD-Assistant CC BY-NC 4.0, code only partly released; ShapeAssembly Brown non-commercial-product licence.
- No licence files for CADCodeVerify (data only), Query2CAD or BlenderAlchemy.
- The 2026 papers (ReliCAD, Embodied CAD, PrimitiveCAD, StepCAD, SEIG, VIGA) exist as described; VIGA does have a project page.
- None of the agentic or program-synthesis papers tests on real partial scans of household objects with mm-level metrics. Only CAD-Recode and cadrille use real scans (CC3D, mechanical parts).

**Bearing on the user's question (are the meshes case by case?)**
- The verified literature supports this split: a fixed, typed part library (lathe, extrude, board, wire-rack), parameters fitted by an optimiser, and a GT-free fit-to-observation selector. Our pipeline already does this; what is still done by hand is writing new fitters.
- Automating that authoring step (ShapeLib-style multi-proposal validation, or FunSearch/AlphaEvolve-style evolution scored by obs_fidelity, which the report missed) is plausible but unproven [H]. Falsifying test: auto-authored fitters for held-out object types fail to match the hand-written prim_* fitters in a pre-registered scan round.
- The thin-sheet bias of obs_fidelity is a known risk for any automated search that uses it as the reward.

**Not verified:** CADEvolve and EvoCAD (the report is truncated there), the cadrille ICLR 2026 venue, and the AlphaEvolve arXiv ID.

No repo files were edited and nothing was run against the scans. Licence and README files went to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/90d4009c-b597-536b-9d55-58f81afca135/scratchpad/licchk (empty) or were read straight to stdout.

methods.name: obs_points.py: observed object-frame stereo points (shared front end)
methods.cpu_feasible: Yes, CPU only. Needs the public FoundationStereo depth cache from the HF store (0.3-0.9 GB per episode) plus our tracks and hands. Eval depth was never cached, so today it runs on public episodes only.
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: Built for this. It removes a table band, hand and forearm capsules and other tracked objects, and keeps a voxel only if it has enough hit frames and is not seen through from other views. [D, existing] median 0.85-1.9 mm from the scans; 59-90 % of the scan within 3 mm. Exceptions: rack ep26 28 % and board 1 ep23 16 %. Undersides are never seen.
methods.output: npz with pts (N,3), cam (camera centre per point), frame, plus hit/free voxel grids and args, in our track (object) frame
methods.fit_to_our_problem: The generic input for every part fitter and for the selector. It works for any object that has a track and a depth cache. The beige cup has no usable points (ep11 track wrong at frame 0). The spoon has no public episode.
methods.reported_accuracy: [D] lid 0.85, blue cup 0.89-0.96, dust pan 1.07, board 2 1.29, pitcher 1.30, sweeper 1.37, rack 1.88, pot 1.89 mm median distance to the scan

methods.name: obs_fidelity.py: GT-free selector (observed->mesh plus mesh->observed trimmed means)
methods.cpu_feasible: Yes, seconds to a minute per mesh (300k points, 200k surface samples)
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: Counts mesh->obs only inside the observations' bounding box. Known bias: it prefers thinner sheets wherever the underside is unseen, so it cannot choose a thickness prior.
methods.output: JSON line per mesh: obs_to_mesh_mm, mesh_to_obs_mm, sum_mm (lower is better)
methods.fit_to_our_problem: The automatic chooser among (episode x variant) candidates. Within one family it ranks well. Across families it was wrong once: it preferred fitted handles over TSDF-residual handles where the scans preferred the TSDF ones. Code defects [M, code read]: the docstring offers --icp and --trim, but neither is implemented. A '--trim 0.9' argument would be read as a mesh path. Candidates outside the track frame (generative meshes) therefore cannot be scored yet.
methods.reported_accuracy: [D] Spearman with CD-O 0.85 over 32 pot candidates and 0.5 over 5 cup candidates. It picked the CD-O winner for the cup (0.291). Pot selection margin was 0.009 mm (ep41 fit 3.035 vs ep41 tsdf 3.044; the tsdf scored better against the scan, 0.333 vs 0.342).

methods.licence: own code (this repo); reuses kit registration functions
methods.cpu_feasible: Yes. The 'amb' subcommand reads only our mesh and also works for the spoon (no scan). The 'run' subcommand reads scans and is for diagnostics only.
methods.partial_noisy_real_data: Works on the mesh only
methods.output: amb_mm: how well a flipped or rotated copy of the mesh fits itself. Below about 3 mm means flip risk.
methods.fit_to_our_problem: An automatic gate for the main failure of primitive meshes: registration flips on near-symmetric shapes (boards, the body-only pot, the sweeper).

Counterexamples: library_v3 board 2 (amb 2.57) had 0 flips at its seeds; frame-0 cup lathes (amb 5-6) flipped 7 of 7 because their shape was wrong.

methods.name: lathe_obs.py: closed-profile thin-wall lathe from observed points (axis by line complex + rotational self-consistency, outer/inner by view side, voxel-splat appendages)
methods.cpu_feasible: Yes, a few minutes per object-episode on this 4-core VM [M, rough wall time]

The unseen base is a flat cut; the floor is at base + t unless an observed floor exists. Fails on frame-0-only points (24-30 % coverage).

GT-free probe here [M]: axis rotational consistency was cup ep21 2.2 mm, pot ep41 2.4, dust pan 2.8, sweeper 4.3, pitcher 10.1. obs_fidelity sum against library_v3: pitcher 7.91 vs 7.05, dust pan 5.98 vs 3.64, sweeper 10.29 vs 4.22, so the lathe is worse on all three. key_insights: ANSWER TO THE OWNER [M, code read]: the meshes are about half automated. Generic and automatic today: the front end obs_points.py (any tracked object with depth), the back end (obs_fidelity selection over episode x variant, manifold3d union, the GT-free amb flip check, mesh_metric scoring for diagnostics), the lathe_obs/pot_body body fitters, the marker-ball fitter, and the TSDF/splat residual. Written case by case: the part list of each object. Agents wrote prim_potlid.py (836 lines), prim_rack.py (884) and prim_boards.py (681) after looking at our points and crops. Each then runs unattended with the GT-free selector. The five objects without a kit (pitcher, sweeper, dust pan, spoon, beige cup) need new part types or data, not more tuning.

PART-TYPE COVERAGE [M, code read]. Code that fits generically: thin-wall lathe body (lathe_obs.py for open cups; prim_potlid.pot_body for containers with a floor); marker ball + stem (prim_potlid.markers_from, prim_boards.find_markers); generic residual (TSDF faces via hybrid.py/tsdf_parts, or obs voxel splat in lathe_obs); joint multi-episode merge (prim_rack.joint); union (manifold3d). Semi-generic, needing an axis or a known context: domed sheet of revolution (build_lid); flat straight bar handle (bar_handle); swept strap/arch (arch_strap); single planar slab extrusion with one thickness (prim_boards). Object-specific: rounded-rect tray minus sloped basin, leaning rounded-rect tube, rows of tapered cone pegs (prim_rack); slot from the crossing board's voxel hits (prim_boards). Missing entirely: ring/torus or annulus with a hole (any through-hole: the board outline uses fill_holes + RETR_EXTERNAL); free-form thin sheet/loft; folded sheet walls; curved generalized cylinder; bowl shell; bristle tuft/block; recessed foot; slot or notch detection from colour.

MATRIX row: blue_cup (5 eval pairs; axisymmetric, not an anchor). Needs: thin-wall open-top lathe body (3.2 mm scan wall, scan has no lower inner wall), recessed foot, about 4 marker balls on stems, no handle (crop [M]). Existing code: body YES (lathe_obs). Markers only as voxel splats; markers_from is not wired in and lathe_obs --spheres is a dead flag. Foot NO. Points: ep21 1.20M/93 frames, ep22 1.11M/95 frames, merged ep21+22 2.31M (merge provenance unrecorded). [D] 0.523 -> 0.291 (ep21) / 0.364 (ep22); ADD 10.0 -> 4.1 mm; 0 of 7 flips. NEW [M]: the ep21 lathe lies a median 2.6-2.8 mm from library_v3/blue_cup.glb with no registration (centroid offset 3.3 mm). It is therefore in the library frame like the pot/lid/rack kit meshes and could join the $0 pack swap without eval depth.

MATRIX row: beige_cup (2 pairs). Same parts as the blue cup. Existing code: the same lathe code would apply. Points: NONE, because the ep11 track is wrong at frame 0 (cups on the lap). [D] The approach-2 lathe on our library mesh (non-compliant input) scored 0.730 -> 0.292, but ADD 5.4 -> 8.2 fails. Blocked by data and tracking, not by part types.

MATRIX row: white_pot (6 pairs; anchor in evals 1, 3, 5, 6, 8). Needs: thin-wall lathe with closed floor (scan 3.9 mm; our measure 4.77 mm), long flat bar handle with a hole near the tip, marker balls on stems. Existing code: body YES (pot_axis + pot_body); bar YES, but the hole was not detected; markers YES (4 of 5 float, one spurious mid-handle ball). Points: 8 episodes (41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 2, 26, 27), 2.5-5.6M each. [D] kit 0.342 / ADD 3.05 / 0 of 8 flips. Same body + TSDF-residual handle: better in 8 of 8 episodes.
