Existing code: spoon_template.py, a hand-parameterised loft (not fitted); fit_spoon.py is a skeleton. Points: none (no public episode; eval depth never cached). [E] about 0.18 inferred; no scan, so no diagnostic is possible.

OBJECTS WITH NO WORKING KIT and what blocks each. (1) Blue cup: effectively automated already (lathe_obs + fidelity). It lacks only marker spheres and a foot, and is not yet in the pack. (2) Beige cup: no observed points (ep11 track). (3) Pitcher: wrong part vocabulary. It needs a free-form thin-shell or loft part, or the generative route, which is blocked on code permission and GPU. (4) Sweeper: no ring/torus part, no hole-preserving outline, no bristle part; anchor and flip-prone. (5) Dust pan: no folded-sheet or annulus part; the TSDF is already decent (0.226-0.331). (6) Spoon: no data to fit on public episodes, and eval depth is missing. (7) Boards: the kit exists but fails on registration symmetry and a wrong-identity track; the geometry itself is not the problem.

LESSON thin walls and the floor carry most of the gain [D]: the thick pot variant was worse in 8 of 8 episodes (e.g. ep41 0.342 -> 0.420); the solid cup lathe scored 0.493 vs hollow 0.392; the solid approach-2 pot 0.545 vs 0.319. The lid passed at every thickness from 1.5 to 4.0 mm, so the exact value matters less than a thin sheet.

LESSON the body is the gain, and hand-fitted appendages add about nothing [D]: on the same thin pot body, the generic TSDF-residual handle beat the fitted bar on CD-O and ADD in 8 of 8 episodes; the lid TSDF residual 0.216 vs fitted arch 0.220. Implication for automation [H]: a library of a few generic BODY types plus a generic residual and generic markers captures most of the measured gain. Falsified if an obs-splat residual (compliant) on the pot and lid scores worse than the fitted parts in a pre-registered round.

LESSON episode choice dominates [D]: the pot kit ranges 0.325-0.597 across 8 episodes, the cup 0.291 vs 0.364, and merging cup episodes hurt (0.396), matching 6 of 6 single-episode wins on 22 Oct. The rack's ICP-aligned joint fit was the one exception the selector chose (0.454, against per-episode 0.422-0.509 with worse ADD). Automation must generate per-episode candidates and select, not fuse.

LESSON the selector works within a family and has known blind spots [D]: Spearman 0.85 over 32 pot candidates, but it prefers thinner sheets where the underside is unseen, chose fitted parts over TSDF residuals where the scans disagreed, and decided the pot by a 0.009 mm margin. Unseen thicknesses must therefore stay generic priors, tested over the {1.5, 2.5, 4.0} mm grid with a must-pass-everywhere rule, as in the clean-up round.

LESSON a name-free family choice is unreliable, and name-based choice is allowed [D/M]: the approach-2 lathe gate falsely passed the dust pan and spoon. Here, rotational consistency puts the dust pan (2.8 mm) next to the pot (2.4) [M]. Object names are a permitted input (CLAUDE.md; approach2 §4; lit §5.4), and the owner said on 22 Oct that 'generalised automatic rules' are OK. So name -> template, with every number fitted to our points, is the defensible automation.

LESSON registration symmetry is the failure mode of primitives [D]: every board candidate had amb 2.5-2.6 mm and flipped; the body-only pot (amb 3.21) flipped 2 of 8. Asymmetric details (slots, notches, handles, marker layout) anchor the frame, and primitives that symmetrise a shape remove them. The GT-free amb check should run on every automated candidate, alongside fidelity.

LESSON leak firewall [work log 27 Oct]: scan-measured wall thicknesses in an agent brief became code priors (rack T_WALL 2.5 mm, lid 2.5 mm, upright cup holder). Any automated or agent-written template must be designed blind to [D] numbers. Its priors must be generic grids, and GT-free fidelity must pick shape options; fidelity rejected the scan-informed upright cup holder.

LESSON frames and eval [D/M]: meshes built from points along our public tracks land in library_v3's object frame (pot, lid, rack 2-4 mm; blue cup 2.6-2.8 mm [M here]). Library-style swaps therefore need no eval depth. Per-eval-episode rebuilds need eval depth (about $2-4 GPU), and frame-0-only data fails (1.1-1.3 cm, 7 of 7 flips). Estimated effect if hidden scans match public ones [E]: pot + lid + rack 0.402 -> 0.367; adding the ep21 blue-cup lathe (5 pairs x -0.232 / 36) -> about 0.335.

LESSON compliance carry-over: the observed points come from sweep tracks seeded with library_v2 (tier P1), and the kit's 'tsdf' residual variants copy library_v3 faces fused along scan-templated tracks (deny-listed). An automated pipeline should prefer obs-only residuals (voxel splat) and record the track tier.

CODE DEFECTS that matter for automation [M, code read]: obs_fidelity documents --icp/--trim but implements neither ('--trim 0.9' would be read as a mesh path); lathe_obs --spheres is a dead flag; prim_boards' outline cannot keep through-holes; markers_from leaves floating balls (no contact or stem snapping); the pot handle hole detector found nothing. Probe outputs from this synthesis (lathes for pitcher, dust pan, sweeper, cup, pot; fidelity; frame check): /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/90d4009c-b597-536b-9d55-58f81afca135/scratchpad/synth_probe/ and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/90d4009c-b597-536b-9d55-58f81afca135/scratchpad/obs_census.py. None read scans; none were scored against scans.
top_claims_to_verify: Hidden eval scans are close enough to the public scans that the public [D] gains transfer: pot + lid + rack swap 0.402 -> 0.367, plus the blue-cup ep21 lathe -> about 0.335 [E]. Only one consistency point exists: the eval-8 beige swap moved the board by the predicted -0.0035. Check: on the next pack, compare the uploaded CD-O delta with the prediction.

The ep21 blue-cup lathe can replace library_v3 in the 5 blue-cup eval pairs without eval depth because it shares library_v3's object frame (median 2.6-2.8 mm, centroid 3.3 mm [M here]). Unverified: whether a 3 mm frame offset between the tracked mesh (library_v3) and the submitted mesh costs anything on the pose boards. ADD 10.0 -> 4.1 mm [D] suggests not. Also unverified: whether ep21 (chosen by fidelity over n=5) is robust.

Generic residual appendages are as good as hand-fitted parts, so automation needs body fitters, not appendage fitters. This holds for the pot in 8 of 8 episodes and is within 0.005 cm on the lid [D], but it was shown only with library_v3 TSDF faces (non-compliant). Test: rebuild the pot and lid with the obs-only voxel splat and score them in a pre-registered round.

obs_fidelity is a valid automatic selector across episodes and part families. Measured: Spearman 0.85 within the pot family (n=32) and 0.5 on cups (n=5). Known biases: thin-sheet preference, preferring fitted parts over TSDF residuals, 0.009 mm decision margins. Test: pool all existing scored candidates (pot, lid, rack, boards, cups) and check that it picks the best or second-best per object on at least 80 % of objects.

amb < 3 mm (GT-free self-ambiguity) predicts registration flips well enough to gate automated meshes. Supporting: boards at 2.5-2.6 all flipped; body-only pot at 3.21 flipped 2 of 8. Counterexamples: library board 2 at 2.57 had 0 flips; frame-0 cup lathes at 5-6 flipped 7 of 7. Test: flip-prediction AUC over all candidates already scored in results/ (no new scan scoring needed).
open_questions: Owner decision: add the ep21 blue-cup lathe (5 pairs, the largest per-object gain, 0.523 -> 0.291 [D]) to the $0 packed-mesh swap with the pot, lid and rack? It was not in the 0.367 estimate. Same question as before: packed mesh only, or also the simulator copy (GPU re-run)?

What does 'automated' need to mean for the owner? Option (a): name-selected templates whose numbers are all fitted GT-free. Names are allowed, and we have about 6-8 templates for 11 objects. Option (b): a name-free part-proposal step, clustering residuals and testing each cluster against sphere, plane, cylinder, torus and strap shapes. Our evidence says name-free family gating misfires (dust pan vs pot).

Provenance of obs/ep21+22_blue_cup.npz: it has no 'args' key, and a scan-alignment *_align.npz sits beside it. Was it a plain concatenation in the shared track frame, or did anything use the alignment? This must be settled before anyone reuses it.

Pitcher: which representation should an automated builder use for a free-form watering-can shell? Options: a two-sided offset surface from points (mid-surface + thickness), a loft of cross-sections along a curved spine, generate-then-fit (needs third-party code permission and GPU), or keep the TSDF and only close its holes (1 pair, but the eval-20 anchor)?

Sweeper and dust pan: both need a ring or annulus-with-hole part and a hole-preserving outline (RETR_CCOMP instead of fill_holes + RETR_EXTERNAL). Will rebuilding these anchor objects raise flip risk? Their library amb is 3.25 (sweeper) and 6.21 (dust pan).

Boards: can identity-safe tracks be produced for ep23 (board 2's track looks like board 1 rotated 180°)? Can the slot be detected GT-free from colour, since the dark line shows in the crop but not in the depth? Both are hypotheses to test before another board round.

Beige cup: can the ep11 track be repaired (frame-0 failure, cup on the lap) to give observed points? If not, the only lathe route uses the non-compliant library mesh (approach 2: 0.292 but ADD 8.2 fails).

Spoon: with no public data, what GT-free acceptance rule should a fitted spoon meet (stereo residual p90 <= 3 mm, held-out silhouette IoU, 0 flips over 40 seeds), and will the owner fund the eval-depth run (about $2-4) that any fit needs?

Which surfaces should an automated builder emit where the scanner probably did not see (lower inner walls, undersides)? The blue-cup scan lacks its lower inner wall, and CD-O's RMS-radius scale punishes a wrong area distribution (0.382 vs 0.316 at true scale [D]). lathe_obs has a --floor observed option, but no [D] result is recorded for it.

Should the generic thickness-prior grid {1.5, 2.5, 4.0} mm with a must-pass-everywhere rule become the standing rule for all never-seen sheets (lid underside, rack floor, dust-pan underside, sweeper bristle base)?
obs_fidelity needs its documented --icp before generative or other off-frame candidates can enter the selector. Should it also gain a held-out silhouette term (lit §7) to reduce the thin-sheet bias?

designs.name: Peel-and-select kit of parts: generic part library, residual peeling, depth-render selection
pipeline_steps: S1 Episode QC gate (generic, new, about 60 lines). Split each episode's frames into two halves and build points for each half. Register half to half with trimmed ICP (prim_rack.icp_align). Reject the episode if rotation > 3 deg, offset > 3 mm or overlap < 50 % [H thresholds]. Target: catch wrong or identity-swapped tracks (beige cup ep11 frame 0, board 2 ep23) before fitting. Single episodes are the unit, because fusion lost on 6/6 objects and on the blue cup [D]. Joint fits (prim_rack.joint, generalised) enter only as extra candidates.

S2 Preprocess. 1.5 mm voxel dedupe (load_obs). Normals oriented to the camera (lathe_obs.normals) and view classes. Up = towards the cameras / the table normal. Object scale s = robust RMS radius of the points. Every later window is a fraction of s or of the fitted part size; this replaces the 60 mm handle reach, the 40-80 mm flange, the 15-35 mm dome, the 50 mm arch, NFACE 1500 and T_MAX 6 mm.

S6 Structure search (residual peeling + beam). For each body hypothesis (top 3 per family):
1. Fit the body.
2. Take residual points more than max(4 mm, 2 sigma) outside it.
3. Cluster them (prim_potlid.clusters, 3 mm voxels).
4. For each cluster try every part family, plus 'leave out' and 'TSDF patch'.
5. Accept the change that most improves the S8 score.
6. Attach the part by contact (<= 2 mm) or a snap constraint: coaxial, coplanar, equal radius (GlobFit-style [L]).
7. Recurse on the new residual.
Beam width 4, at most 8 parts plus markers. A fit that ends on a parameter bound is rejected: [M] the rack fitter on the pitcher and sweeper, and the lid strap on the dust pan, were silent bound-hit failures. Every candidate is unioned with manifold3d and passed through the kit's budget_mesh (<= 4096 faces) before scoring.

S7 Never-seen geometry: declared priors, never selected by fidelity.
- Base: walls extend to the table plane (obs_points removes the bottom 8 mm) and close with a plate of thickness t.
- Containers: closed floor.
- Sheets with an unseen underside: underside = top - t.
- t comes from two-wall / two-face evidence when at least 3 bins or a relative point count see both sides. Otherwise every value of a generic grid {1.5, 2.5, 4.0} mm is built, and the object must pass at every value.
Reason [M, this run]: standard fidelity prefers the thinnest lid through noise absorption, and the culled version is flat, so neither carries information about t.

S8 GT-free selection over (bodies x structures x episodes x joint) + library_v3:
- Primary: z-buffered depth-render agreement on held-out frames (fit on even frames, score on odd). Render each candidate at our tracked pose with crops.py geometry() and a z-buffer splat (render_ids). Per pixel in the union of rendered and observed object masks, take |delta depth| capped at 10 mm; add a free-space violation share (rendered surface more than 10 mm in front of observed depth).
- Secondary: untrimmed recall at 3 mm. The 90 % trim of obs_fidelity hides missing parts below 10 % of the points, and handles are 5-7 % of the pot's points.
- Complexity: + lambda * k, with lambda calibrated GT-free on synthetic recoveries. Resample points from our own kit meshes through each episode's real coverage and noise residuals, and require the search to recover the known part count.
- Hard gates: pipeline/mesh_gates.py flip check of the candidate against library_v3 and against itself at the eval seeds (fail on rotation > 90 deg), watertight, <= 4096 faces.
- Optional tie-break: silhouette IoU against masks seeded from projected obs points, not from crops.py's GrabCut, which is seeded by library_v3 and would favour it.

S9 Output. Per object: one mesh plus a JSON of parts, parameters, k and every candidate's scores, with the code SHA. Frozen code rebuilds the eval library from public episodes. The spoon has no public episode, so it runs only on eval-episode points once eval depth exists. That is inference, with no tuning.
designs.what_stays_manual:
Being honest about where people are still needed:
1. The part vocabulary. 'No object names in code' is not 'no object knowledge': the 10 part types were chosen by people who have seen these 11 objects. A new kind of object (bristles, hinges, cloth) needs a new part written by a person or agent.
2. The priors for geometry we never see: the thickness grid, the table-contact base and closed floors. Also the fact that the scans are partial (no lower inner wall on the blue cup) and how that interacts with the scorer's area-weighted scale. Points cannot settle these ([M], the lid t-grid), so they stay declared human choices, guarded by the pass-at-every-value rule.
3. Global constants: the stereo noise scale, the residual distance, the 7 mm marker radius, the QC thresholds, beam width and lambda. Lambda is calibrated on synthetic data, but the protocol for doing so is a human design.
4. Upstream tracks. The beige cup (ep11 frame 0) and board 2 (ep23 identity) need re-tracking; no mesh fitter can fix a wrong track. Eval depth for the spoon (and for any eval-only rebuild) needs a GPU job and the owner's go-ahead.
5. Writing the pre-registration and reading the scan round: the pass/fail decision per object, visual QA on the eval-view page, and the owner's submission decision, including whether to swap the simulator copy (a GPU re-run) or only the packed mesh ($0).
6. Diagnosing a failed object and deciding whether to add a part type or fall back to library_v3.
7. The selector itself. Because no point-based score was right on all 8 objects, the final rule needs one human design pass and must then be frozen before scans are touched.

designs.cost:
Cost is $0 for the build: CPU only, on this 4-core VM.

Measured [M]:
- 26 fitter runs: 2-191 s each, 1,080 s in total, under contention from another process on the VM. 3 crashed, 23 wrote meshes.
- Scoring 48 candidates with 2 scorers took about 25 min.

Estimates [E]:
- Search: about 100-300 part fits per (object, episode), so 10-60 min each. For about 25 public (object, episode) units that is 5-20 CPU-hours.
- Depth-render scoring: about 30 held-out frames x candidates, roughly 1-3 CPU-hours.
- Pre-registered scan round: CPU, $0. About 9-21 scorings (one per selected candidate, plus t-grid siblings).

GPU: not needed for the 10 public-episode objects. Optional:
- eval depth for the spoon: ops/jobs/eval_perc.sh, about $2-4, owner go-ahead;
- re-tracking beige cup ep11 and boards ep23: part of the normal perception job cost;
- a simulator-copy re-run if the owner swaps more than the packed mesh.
designs.effort_estimate:
About 7-10 agent-days [E]:
- Refactor existing generic code into one module: loading, unified markers, relative windows, clusters, union, budget_mesh. 1 day.
- New or generalised parts: P4 folded shell, P6 centreline fitting, P7 lattice sharing, P8 superquadric, an arclength profile for P1, face-sign-free P5. 3 days.
- QC gate. 0.5 day.
- Beam search with bound-hit rejection. 1 day.
- Depth-render scorer on held-out frames, free-space term and flip-gate integration. 1.5 days.
- Synthetic lambda calibration. 1 day.
- Pre-registered round, audit and write-up. 1 day.

The GT-free selector check on the frozen 48-candidate matrix (falsification part A) can run after day 2-3, before the remaining work is spent.

risks.risk: The GT-free selector mis-ranks structures across families. [M] here, each of 5 point-based scores fails 1-2 of 8 objects: standard on rack and sweeper; culled on cup and rack; F3 on lid and rack; recall on dust pan; capped mean on rack.
risks.mitigation: Use z-buffered depth-render agreement on held-out frames as the primary score; library_v3 is always a candidate; apply the per-object pass rule; run falsification part A on the frozen matrix before building more.

risks.risk: Generic parts fit wrong structures silently. [M] 23/26 wrong-template runs exited 0 with watertight meshes; the rack fitter hit its bounds on the pitcher and sweeper; the lid strap fitted a phantom arch on the dust pan.
risks.mitigation: Reject any fit that ends on a bound; each part must keep support across frames; a residual must shrink to accept a part; synthetic recovery test with known part counts.

risks.risk: Registration flips. An automated structure that is better on CD-O loses the asymmetric cues (slot, handle, markers) that set the kit's PCA-start ICP; [D] board 1 scored 0.189 but had 1/6 flips.
risks.mitigation: Hard flip gate (mesh_gates.py) at the eval seeds; prefer candidates that keep markers and handles; 0-flip pass rule.

risks.risk: Priors for never-seen geometry (wall and underside thickness, base, partial scans) drive CD-O more than the fitted parts do, and the area-weighted scale normalisation amplifies them.
risks.mitigation: t grid with pass-at-every-value; never select t by fidelity ([M] lid); report a CD-O decomposition (cdo_decomp.py) in the round.

risks.risk: Bad tracks (beige cup ep11, board 2 ep23) give wrong points, and no fitter can recover from that.
risks.mitigation: S1 half-split QC gate; fall back to library_v3; re-track as a separate, owner-approved GPU job.

risks.risk: Leakage at the selector level: the selector is chosen after seeing which scores agree with existing public [D] orders.
risks.mitigation: Declare it, freeze the selector in a commit, validate on fresh search candidates, and never override a selection after scoring.

risks.risk: The search is too slow or too large on 4 cores.
risks.mitigation: Slippage ordering, beam width 4, at most 8 parts, cached axes (--axis_cache), 1.5 mm voxels.

risks.risk: Stereo artefacts (double layers, edge bleeding) create phantom parts.
risks.mitigation: Free-space violation term from the render; minimum support across frames; the same 7 mm marker prior everywhere.

risks.risk: Spoon and other eval-only objects stay uncovered without eval depth.
risks.mitigation: Keep the spoon template; run the pipeline on eval points only after an approved eval_perc job.

riskiest_assumptions: A GT-free score exists that orders structures from different families the way CD-O does. [M] here, none of 5 point-based scores manages it on 8 objects, each failing in a different place. The design bets on held-out depth-render agreement, which models occlusion (rack) and phantom or missing parts (dust pan, sweeper). This is untested.

Residual peeling over about 10 generic part types recovers a usable part list from our 1-2 mm noisy, one-sided points (28-90 % coverage) without object names. No hand template has yet been reproduced by a search. [M] Schnabel-style RANSAC explains only 24-60 % of points in 8-83 fragments, and the existing fitters land on their bounds when the structure is wrong.

Never-seen geometry can be closed by object-agnostic priors (table-contact base, closed floors, a t grid) without per-object choices, and the partial, double-walled hidden scans do not punish those closures through the area-weighted scale normalisation.
designs.falsification_experiment:
Part A (GT-free selector test, $0, before most of the build).
- Freeze the depth-render selector (score, lambda, thresholds) in a commit. Then score the existing 48-candidate matrix in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/90d4009c-b597-536b-9d55-58f81afca135/scratchpad/design_classic (matrix/*.glb, plus the library and hand meshes listed in score_all.sh) on held-out frames.
- Reference first choice per object:
  - hand fit for cup ep21, pot ep41, lid ep2, rack ep26 (joint) and board 1 ep24, from existing [D];
  - library_v3 for sweeper ep31, pitcher ep22 and dust pan ep39, from [E].
- Falsified if the reference is ranked first on <= 6 of 8 objects, i.e. no better than the point scores measured here, which got 6-7 of 8.

Part B (blind structure recovery, GT-free).
- Strip object names (shuffled IDs) and run the search on the 9 public objects that have points.
- Falsified if, on fewer than 4 of the 5 objects with hand templates (pot, lid, rack, blue cup, board 1), it reproduces the hand body family and the appendage count to within 1.
- Also falsified if, on synthetic recoveries (points resampled from our own kit meshes through each episode's real coverage and noise), it misses the known part count on more than 1 of 5.

Part C (pre-registered scan round). Falsified if either:
- it passes the rule (CD-O <= lib - 0.03 cm, ADD <= lib + 1 mm, 0 flips) on fewer than 4 of the 9 public objects; or
- it is worse than the hand kit fits by more than 0.03 cm on any of pot, lid or rack.

If A fails, the router is not trustworthy, and the honest fallback is the current practice: hand-written templates per object type plus GT-free fitting.
designs.pre_registration_sketch:
1. Before any scan is read, commit:
   - the code SHA and the selector definition (depth-render score, recall term, lambda and how it was calibrated, the gates);
   - the t grid {1.5, 2.5, 4.0} mm, the QC thresholds and the beam settings;
   - the list of public episodes per object.
   Then run S0-S9 blind on the 9 objects with public points and commit a manifest: all candidates with their GT-free scores, the one selected candidate per object, and its t-grid siblings where t is a prior.
2. Integrity evidence, also committed:
   - a grep of the method code for scan, mocap, align and parquet-pose paths;
   - an strace -e openat log of the generation run showing no reads under the scans directory, *_align.npz or the parquets;
   - an independent re-run that reproduces the selection exactly.
3. Scan scoring with mesh_metric.py at the eval seeds: exactly one scoring per selected candidate (plus its t siblings), with ADD and flips on >= 6 seeds. Every scoring is logged with its command and SHA; the expected total is 9-21 scorings.
4. Pass rule per object, the same as ours: CD-O <= library_v3 - 0.03 cm, ADD <= library_v3 + 1 mm, 0 flips. Objects whose t comes from the prior must pass at every grid value; the middle value is submitted.
5. Secondary, declared in advance and never used to choose: the Spearman correlation between the GT-free score and CD-O over the scored meshes, and the Part A/B outcomes.
6. No overrides. A failing object keeps library_v3, or the earlier passing hand-kit mesh for pot, lid and rack. A change needs a new pre-registered round on public data only. Nothing is ever tuned on eval.
7. After passing: rebuild the eval library from the public episodes with the same SHA (the objects are identical, so no eval depth is needed). Swap only the passing objects. The owner decides between a $0 pack-only swap and a GPU simulator-copy re-run. Update STATUS.md and the work log, and commit the exact code for the submission.

designs.name: Frozen part-program loop: an agent writes a short program in a fixed part language, an optimiser fits it to our points, and a GT-free selector picks among frozen candidates
designs.summary:
Short answer to "are the meshes made case by case?": yes, today they are. The kit-of-parts meshes were made by agents writing one fitter per object type. The audits counted 33-55 % of each fitter's lines as knowledge of one object [M audit]: the part list, the "handle = cluster reaching > 60 mm beyond the body" rule, the lid's 40-80 mm flange window, and so on. Once a fitter exists, fitting and selection are automatic and GT-free.

The design below automates the authoring step itself, as a frozen and logged protocol:
1. Build a generic part language once (about 10 part types with typed parameters), from the generic code we already have.
2. Per object, an agent with vision (Claude through the API, firewalled from the repo) looks at our colour crops, renders of our observed points and an automatic "evidence card", and writes a 10-30 line program in that language.
3. A deterministic optimiser fits every continuous parameter to our points.
4. The agent revises the program for up to 8 rounds, using GT-free feedback only: fidelity, free-space violations, residual images, physical checks, and a registration-flip probe.
5. Four independent sessions per object, plus a no-agent "router" control arm, give the candidates. They are gated and selected GT-free on held-out episodes, then frozen and committed before one pre-registered scan round.

The human design effort moves from about 300-400 object-specific lines per object to a part vocabulary written once. The vocabulary is still design knowledge; the honest gain is that it is written once, while the per-object choice is made by a logged loop and checked against a control.

Measured here for this design [M]: $0, CPU, our own points and existing meshes only, no scans read. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/90d4009c-b597-536b-9d55-58f81afca135/scratchpad/autoloop_probe/fs_fidelity.py; outputs are the *.jsonl files in the same folder.
- **A free-space gate rejects wrong templates by a wide margin.** It uses the 4 mm free/hit vote grids that obs_points.py already stores in every obs file. fs_frac is the share of mesh area lying where our depth saw empty space.
  - Rule: fs_frac must be at most library_v3's fs_frac + 5 percentage points.
  - It accepted 9/9 hand-fit and variant meshes: lid t1.5/2.5/4.0 fit and two TSDF variants, cup lathe, pot fit, rack joint v1/v2.
  - It rejected 11/11 wrong-template meshes: dust pan as board (2), pot, lid and lathe; pitcher as pot, lathe and rack; sweeper as lathe and rack; rack as lathe.
  - Wrong templates sit at 19-61 %, against 0.75-7.4 % for the library meshes of those objects. Example, pitcher lathe: obs_fidelity margin 7.91 vs 7.05 mm, fs_frac 27.8 vs 6.3 %.
  - The threshold was set after looking at these 20 meshes, so on new candidates it is [H].
- **obs_fidelity cannot decide library_v3 versus a structured mesh.** Over all 5 rack episodes it prefers library_v3 (5.53 mm) over the prim joint meshes (5.94 and 6.12 mm). The scans say the prim is better (0.555 to 0.456 cm [D]). Restricting mesh-to-observation distances to observed voxels flips the rack (2.95 vs 3.89). It does not remove the thin-sheet bias on the lid thickness grid (1.32 / 1.53 / 1.97 mm for 1.5 / 2.5 / 4.0 mm), because the 4 mm voxels are coarser than the thickness. So:
  - the GT-free selector only ranks structured candidates against each other;
  - library versus new is decided by the scan pass rule;
  - unseen thicknesses stay a prior grid.
- **Existing selected fits are not single bodies.** trimesh splits them into 2-5 pieces: pot fit 5, lid 2, cup lathe 5, rack 3. These are floating marker balls (the README also notes floating balls). So a "parts attached" check needs stems.
- **The colour-crop masks are seeded from library_v3's silhouette** (crops.py l.3-5, l.118-130, GrabCut). A silhouette-IoU term against them would favour library_v3, so the masks must be re-seeded from our projected observed points.
- **The repo itself leaks scan numbers.** README l.29 quotes scan wall thicknesses (cup 2.4-3.2, pot 3.9, lid 1.8, pitcher 2.2, rack fins about 2.5 mm). An authoring agent with repo access would see them, and this happened once before (work log 2026-10-27). So authoring must run with no file access.

Expected result [E]:
- Overall CD-O about 0.27-0.34 cm, against 0.402 submitted.
- The top of that range equals what existing work already gives: the hand-made pot, lid and rack meshes plus the blue-cup lathe.
- The loop's own value is coverage of the pitcher, dust pan, sweeper and the cup handle, plus less hand design. Its marginal CD-O gain over existing work is about 0-0.045 cm [E].
- The spoon (10 of 36 pairs, about 0.18 inferred, no public scan) and the beige cup (bad track) cap what any mesher can reach; the leaders are at 0.112-0.154.
pipeline_steps: 0. FREEZE AND FIREWALL (once). Commit the part-language interpreter, prompts, model ID and effort, budgets, gates, selection rule and prior grids before any run. Authoring runs as a Claude API tool loop. The agent's only tools are evidence(), fit(program), feedback(candidate) and submit(program): no file system, no repo, no web. A script builds the input bundle per object from an allowlist: obs npz for public episodes, re-seeded crops, point renders, the object name, the part-language documentation. A leak check greps every prompt and every agent output for the scan numbers quoted in the docs (README l.29) and for scan, mocap or align paths; any hit voids that session. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset on this VM [M], so the owner must supply credentials and approve the spend.

1. EVIDENCE CARD (deterministic, no agent). Steps: obs_points.py (exists) -> 1.5 mm voxel downsample -> normals (lathe_obs.normals) -> residual-free surface segmentation -> per-segment family hints. The hints come from three sources: slippage analysis (Gelfand-Guibas: rotational = lathe, translational = slab or extrusion, none = blob), RANSAC planes, cylinders and spheres (Schnabel style; our own numpy version gave 24-60 % explained [M, earlier probe]), and lathe rotational consistency. Also computed: marker balls (merge prim_potlid set A and prim_boards set B into one detector), table plane and rest frames, a coverage map. Outputs: JSON plus 8-12 images (4 point renders by normal and by observation count, 2-4 crops with re-seeded masks, residual cluster map). The agent sees this card, never raw thresholds.

3. FIT (deterministic, CPU). Each part's initialiser comes from the existing fitter code. Then a joint robust refinement: scipy least_squares, soft-L1, on observed-to-mesh distance on the training episodes, plus a free-space penalty per part. Multi-start from the evidence-card seeds; fixed RNG seeds. A program, the interpreter commit and the seeds reproduce the mesh exactly.

5. AGENT LOOP (arm V). Per object, K = 4 independent sessions (2 prompt variants x 2 repeats; temperature cannot be set from API version 2026-10-21 [L, claude-api skill], so repeats are the seeds). At most 8 rounds per session. A session stops after 2 rounds without a 2 % improvement. Keep each session's final and best-intermediate program, at most 8 per object. Log every program, transcript and token usage.

6. ROUTER CONTROL (arm R, no agent). Enumerate single-family programs on every object: lathe + residual sweeps/patches, slab, plate_set, drafted_shell + sweeps, and patch-only. Same fit, same gates. This is the deterministic router the audits proposed. It tells us whether the agent adds anything.

7. PRIOR GRID. Every surviving candidate is rebuilt at each unseen-thickness grid value {1.5, 2.5, 4.0} mm (sweeper class {4, 8, 13}?: fix the grid from generic household ranges before running, not from the scan). Selection uses the middle value; the pass rule must hold at all values (as in the lid and rack clean-up round).

8. GT-FREE SELECTION (frozen rule).
- Gates: watertight; one body after stems, or markers attached; fs_frac at most library_v3's per-episode median + 5 pp; no more than 20 % of parameters on bounds; flip probe with 0 off-identity optima; rest check passed for static objects.
- Rank by held-out obs_fidelity sum_mm plus lambda x number of parameters (lambda pre-registered, e.g. 0.01 mm per parameter). Held out means episodes the loop never saw: pot 8 episodes, rack 5, lid 2, blue cup 2, pitcher 21/22, sweeper 18/31, dust pan 18/39/40. Missing obs files are built first from the store's public depth.
- library_v3 and the hand-made meshes are reference rows only, never selectable by this rule.

9. FREEZE AND COMMIT. Commit the programs (part-language text), fitted-parameter JSON, meshes up to 10 MB, transcripts, selection JSON and code commit. Write a work-log pre-registration entry, then STATUS. Only then go to the scan round.

10. SCAN ROUND (separate, pre-registered, owner go-ahead). Run mesh_metric.py once per frozen candidate and grid value. The decision uses only the selected candidate. The other scorings validate the selector (Spearman per object). An object swaps into the eval pack only if it passes. The spoon has no scan: report it GT-free only and keep the template unless the owner decides otherwise.

11. EVAL. Meshes are per object, built once from public episodes, in the track or library object frame (check: median distance to library_v3 under 5 mm, as for the prim meshes). Pack swap at $0. Whether to rebuild the simulator copy is an open owner question (README sec. 9).
designs.what_stays_manual:
Honest list.
1. **The part vocabulary and its interpreter, written once.** Deciding that handles are sweeps, that folded sheets are plate sets, and so on, is still human (agent) design knowledge, now applied to every object rather than per object. Most of it is a refactor of existing generic and family code (about 38 % generic plus 19 % family lines in prim_potlid and prim_boards [M audit]). New pieces: sweep centreline fitting, plate_set, the unified marker detector and the evidence card.
2. **Protocol choices, made and frozen before any run:** prompts, gates and their thresholds (the fs gate threshold was picked on 20 known meshes), the selection weight lambda, budgets.
3. **Priors for geometry we never see** (undersides, tray floor, lid thickness). Our points cannot measure them [D: tmeas_lid failed]. They stay fixed grids with the "pass at every value" rule.
4. **Track problems are outside this design:** the ep23 board-identity track, the beige-cup ep11 frame-0 track, and the pitcher's track/registration (reference vs mocap 0.571 on ep21, from the ledger).
5. **Owner decisions:**
   - API credentials and spend go-ahead;
   - go-ahead for the scan round;
   - the spoon (no scan, so the pass rule cannot apply);
   - pack-only versus simulator rebuild.
6. **An independent audit** that the firewall held (no scan-derived number in any prompt or output), and of the selection, as in the clean-up round.
7. **Reading the visual output once before submission** (sanity, not tuning). Any change after scan scores means a new pre-registered version.

The agent removes the per-object choice of part list and part-finding rules (the 33-55 % object-specific code). It does not remove the design of the vocabulary, the priors or the protocol.

designs.cost:
**CPU (this VM, 4 cores, $0 marginal):**
- One fit takes 24 s to 2 min 19 s per fitter run [M audit timings].
- Agent arm, about 10 objects x (4 sessions x 8 rounds + 3 grid rebuilds of finalists): about 400 fits, about 10 CPU-h, about 3 h wall [E].
- Router arm: about 100 fits, about 2.5 CPU-h [E].
- Evidence cards and the free-space probe: minutes per object [M: the probe ran 1-4 min per object on 2-8 episodes].
- Scan round: about 100-150 mesh_metric scorings, about 2-4 CPU-h [E].

**Agent API** (Claude Opus 5.5 at $4 / $20 per M input/output tokens, cache reads $0.20 [L, claude-api skill price table cached 2026-10-06]):
- About 320 calls, each about 25k input tokens (8-12 images at about 1.2-1.6k tokens each [E], program, panel, history) and about 8k output including adaptive thinking.
- That is about 8 M input tokens ($8-32 depending on prompt caching) plus about 2.6 M output ($51): **about $60-85 per full run [E]**.
- The Stage A reproduction test alone (pot, lid, rack) costs about $10-20 [E]. Sonnet 5.5 would be about half, at unknown quality.

**GPU:** none needed. Optional about $2-4 [E, README sec. 8 rate] only if held-out public episodes (pitcher 21, sweeper 18, dust pan 18/40) lack depth in the HF store.

**Total about $60-110 [E].** It needs owner credentials (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset here [M]) and, under the spending rule, a stated plan and the owner's go-ahead first.

risks.risk: The agent invents or mislabels parts: ribs or handle holes seen in crops but not in depth, wrong relations. LLMs 'misattribute constraints' (ShapeLib [L]).
risks.mitigation: Per-part support gate (a part must explain its own points; area in seen-empty space is limited by fs_frac); 4 independent sessions; router arm R as control; the agent cannot set unseen dimensions.

risks.risk: Goodhart: the loop optimises the same GT-free fidelity that selects. It may thin or delete unseen surfaces (the known thin-sheet bias; seen-only scoring does not remove it at 4 mm voxels [M]).
risks.mitigation: Selection only on held-out episodes; closed-body and attachment gates; unseen thickness only from the grid, with pass at every value; complexity penalty; library and hand meshes are references only.

risks.risk: Scan-number leakage into authoring. README l.29 lists scan wall thicknesses, and it happened once before.
risks.mitigation: API tool loop with no file or web access; allowlisted bundle; grep every prompt and output for doc-quoted scan values and forbidden paths; independent auditor; a void session is logged, not silently rerun.

risks.risk: The GT-free selector mis-ranks on new object types. Spearman 0.85 was measured only on pot candidates; sum_mm prefers library_v3 over the [D]-better rack prim (5.53 vs 5.94 mm [M]).
risks.mitigation: Do not let the selector arbitrate library vs new (the scan pass rule does). Measure per-object Spearman in the scan round across all frozen candidates. If the median is below 0.5, report the selector as failed.

risks.risk: Optimiser local minima or parameters stuck on bounds (e.g. the rack template on the pitcher [M audit]).
risks.mitigation: Multi-start from evidence-card seeds; flags for parameters at bounds go back into the feedback; gate at most 20 % of parameters on bounds.

risks.risk: Bad tracks defeat any mesher (beige ep11, board 2 ep23, possibly the pitcher).
risks.mitigation: Exclude them from swaps; fix tracks in a separate work item; the flip probe is a gate.

risks.risk: Authoring is not reproducible: no temperature control from API 2026-10-21 [L].
risks.mitigation: The frozen artifact is the committed program plus interpreter commit plus seeds (bit-exact refit); report the spread across the K sessions; never rerun sessions after seeing scan scores.

risks.risk: Requiring connected parts (marker stems) changes CD-O; current fits float 1-4 balls [M].
risks.mitigation: Score both the connected and the unconstrained variant as grid values; the pass rule must hold for the variant that is submitted.

risks.risk: The new meshes are not in the library object frame used by the eval tracks.
risks.mitigation: Fit in the track frame (as now); gate on a median distance to library_v3 under 5 mm without registration.

risks.risk: Effort or cost overrun; the marginal gain over existing hand meshes is small [E 0-0.045 cm].
risks.mitigation: Stage A go/no-go after about 3-4 days and $10-20; session and round budgets; the router-only fallback costs $0 in API.

risks.risk: Rules challenge: an 'agent-authored' template is argued not to be our own reconstruction.
risks.mitigation: Case (c): generic parts, every number fitted to our points, names only as hints; transcripts kept; no third-party meshes or weights.

riskiest_assumptions: 1. The agent adds value over a deterministic router. With crops and point renders it picks a correct part structure for the objects we have not modelled (pitcher spout and handle, dust-pan folded plates, sweeper block and ring) more often than enumerating single-family programs. No paper shows a 'VLM writes a template, optimiser fits it to real depth' loop near 1 % Chamfer [L, primitives-cad.md sec. 4]. [H] Falsified if arm V's selected candidates pass the scan rule on no more objects than arm R's, or if V cannot reproduce the hand fits GT-free in Stage A.

2. Held-out GT-free signals rank structured candidates in CD-O order on new object types: obs_fidelity sum_mm plus the fs gate plus the flip probe. Evidence so far: Spearman 0.85 on pot candidates only [D]; sum_mm mis-ranks library vs prim on the rack [M]; thin-sheet bias [M]. [H] Falsified if the median per-object Spearman between held-out sum_mm and CD-O over the frozen candidates is below 0.5, or if the selected candidate is worse than the median candidate on at least half the objects.

3. Thin structured meshes, fitted to 60-90 % coverage with prior-filled unseen surfaces, gain CD-O on the unmodelled objects as they did on the cup, pot and lid. The scorer's area-weighted RMS scale normalisation punishes extra or missing surface, and the scans themselves are partial. [H] Falsified if the dust pan and the sweeper both fail the pass rule at every grid value with their best structured program.
designs.falsification_experiment:
**Stage A: GT-free go/no-go** (about $10-20 API, CPU, no scans; run once the part language covers lathe, sor_sheet, slab, drafted_shell, loft, sweep and markers):
- Run arm V (K = 4 sessions, at most 8 rounds) and arm R blind on the white pot, lid and rack, from names, crops and points only.
- Compare held-out sum_mm with the hand-made references [M]: pot 3.035 mm over 8 episodes; lid 1.44 / 1.69 / 2.26 mm at t 1.5 / 2.5 / 4.0; rack 5.94 mm over 5 episodes.
- **The design is falsified (stop) if** no V session gets within 5 % of the hand reference on at least 2 of the 3 objects (the agent cannot even rediscover known structure), or if V never beats R by more than 2 % on any of them (the agent adds nothing: keep the router, drop the agent).
- Secondary [H] check: the fs gate (fs_frac at most library_v3 + 5 pp) must keep every V and R candidate whose structure matches the hand part list, and reject the wrong-family ones.

**Stage B: scan validation** (pre-registered, after the freeze): arms V and R on the 8 scanned objects with usable tracks (blue cup, pot, lid, rack, pitcher, dust pan, sweeper, board 1).
- **Falsified if** V passes the pass rule on fewer than 2 of the 4 newly covered objects (blue-cup handle variant, pitcher, dust pan, sweeper), or on no more objects than R.
- **Also falsified if** the selector fails: median per-object Spearman between held-out GT-free score and CD-O below 0.5.
- The flip-probe hypothesis is tested on the same round: does a GT-free 'off-identity optimum' predict scan flips (sensitivity at least 0.8 on the existing scored board and pot candidates plus the new ones)?

designs.name: Zoo-Fit-Route: off-the-shelf proposal zoo, one generic observation fit, one visibility-aware GT-free router
pipeline_steps:
S1 Track-QA gate, GT-free.
- Drop an episode whose points disagree with the object's other episodes after trimmed ICP (prim_rack.icp_align residual over 1.25x the median), or whose rigid-attachment vote keeps under 50 % of ROI points.
- [H] This removes beige ep11 and board-2 ep23 without a human. Falsified if it keeps either one or drops a pot or rack episode used by the passing fits.
S2a Proposals, CPU, own code, already runnable: superquadric part proposals from sq_probe.py, applied to residual clusters, not whole objects ([M] whole objects lost 9/9).

S2b Proposals, GPU, needs owner permission: Pixal3D-MV (MIT). 4–6 posed RGBA crops plus transforms.json from our track (camera-to-world = inverse object pose, Z-up, view 0 canonical); 2 seeds; output already in our frame.
S2c Proposals, GPU, needs owner permission: SAM 3D Objects (SAM licence, gated HF access), through the organisers' v2d_sam3d wrapper (Apache-2.0). 6 frames x 2 seeds, with our metric pointmap.
S2d Proposals, GPU, needs owner permission: TRELLIS.2 (MIT) or Step1X-3D (Apache-2.0). 2 crops x 2 seeds.

S2e Optional, only after an owner licence decision: cadrille point-cloud-to-CadQuery (weights CC-BY-NC-4.0), K=8 programs, for the boards, dust pan and rack only. MeshCoder only if its gated CC-BY-NC-SA weights are accepted. Hunyuan3D-Omni only if the owner is outside EU/UK/KR.

S3 Placement.
- Pixal3D-MV output: rigid trimmed ICP only, starting from identity.
- Canonical-frame outputs: Sim(3) search (sim3_probe.py: 288 starts, coarse-to-fine, trimmed two-sided Umeyama ICP) plus a term for silhouette IoU along 25 held-out frames of our track.
- Ambiguity gate: if any start within 2 % of the best score sits more than 5 mm ADD away from it, reject the candidate unless its frame came from the generator.

S4 Observation fit.
- trimesh nricp_amberg with high stiffness pulls the generator's surfaces lying within 1 cm of our points onto them; unseen regions keep the generator's geometry.
- For CAD programs (S2e): parse the numeric literals and re-fit them by Nelder-Mead or CMA-ES on the router's fidelity score. The model gives the structure, our optimiser the numbers.
- Add marker balls with prim_potlid.markers_from on residual clusters.
- Union with manifold3d into one watertight mesh, then decimate to at most 4096 faces.

S5 Hybrids, built automatically:
- (a) family-fit body plus generator parts lying outside it (hybrid.py logic, but with a manifold union);
- (b) generator body plus our observed residual (prim_potlid.tsdf_parts).
These cover the lathe-body-plus-generated-handle case without handle code.

S7 Pre-registered public scan round. Score every candidate once with mesh_metric.py at the eval seeds plus 6 or more random seeds (CD-O, ADD, flips) and log the selector's Spearman correlation with CD-O.

S8 Pack and review.
- Pack the passing meshes (public-built, same frame as library_v3): a $0 pack change.
- The simulator copy (GPU re-run) is the owner's decision.
- Render every chosen mesh into the eval-view page for a visual check.
- Update STATUS.md and the work log.

scores.design: Frozen part-program loop: an agent writes a short program in a fixed part language, an optimiser fits it to our points, and a GT-free selector picks among frozen candidates
scores.reasons:
Its protocol is better aligned with the measured evidence on accuracy. The GT-free selector never decides library versus new: [M] sum_mm prefers library over the rack prim, 5.53 vs 5.94 mm. That choice is made by the pre-registered scan pass rule, and selection uses held-out episodes. This protects the 12 already-won pairs (pot, lid, rack) better than design 1's library-in-selector.
It names a concrete CPU path for the beige cup (2 pairs, 0.73-0.86 cm, the worst non-spoon error): obs_points along the existing v3x ep11 track. The fs_frac free-space gate is a real, cheap, measured contribution, and its 9/9 accept and 11/11 reject reproduce exactly.
The gate generalises less well than claimed. New [M] on 25 more matrix candidates:
- it passes the wrong flat board plate on the sweeper (11.48 % vs library 7.39 %, inside +5 pp), and that plate also wins sum_mm (3.27 vs 4.22), so this rule would select it;
- it passes tiny partial plates that cover only a fraction of the object (cup 2.81 %, pot 0.89 %, lid 1.10 %, pitcher 2.65 %): it measures precision only;
- it rejects the single-episode correct-family rack fit (18.9 % vs 4.15 %).
Because library and hand meshes are 'never selectable' and there is no completeness floor, the rule would forward the pitcher's 300 cm² plate fragment (sum_mm 61) as the 'selected' candidate.
The distinguishing component, the VLM-authored program, has zero measured evidence. It costs $60-110 and needs credentials that are not on this VM (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset [M]). It cannot be reproduced exactly. Its marginal CD-O gain is self-estimated at 0-0.045 cm. The overall lower bound of 0.27 cm needs the beige track fixed and every per-object lower bound to hold; without beige the arithmetic gives about 0.31 at best [E]. Spoon (10) is untouched.
fatal_flaws: The selector's measured gate is overfit to the 20 meshes it was tuned on. On fresh matrix candidates it passes a wrong-family sweeper plate that also wins sum_mm, and it rejects a correct-family rack fit. With no recall or completeness floor and library excluded, it forwards wrong or fragmentary 'selected' candidates (pitcher plate fragment, sum_mm 61) into the scan round.

The core novelty, the agent arm, has no measured or literature support near this accuracy ([L] primitives-cad sec. 4 says no such loop is reported near 1 % Chamfer). The router arm R does the generic work at $0. Accuracy gains attributable to the agent are pure [H].

Held-out selection is thinner than listed. [M] lid ep0 obs are off-frame by 23-26 mm, so the lid has no usable held-out episode. Pitcher ep21, sweeper ep18 and dust pan ep18/40 have no obs files yet and depend on public depth being in the store.

The plan scores 100-150 candidates against scans. It is allowed as validation, but it multiplies the forking paths unless the 'decision uses only the selected candidate' rule is enforced by a committed manifest.
best_ideas_to_graft: The fs_frac free-space gate from the obs files' own 4 mm free/hit grids, used together with design 1's untrimmed recall. New [M]: fs gate, then rec3 >= library rec3 - 0.05, then rank by sum_mm picks the reference on 8 of 8 matrix objects (post hoc, [H] on new candidates).
Library versus new is decided only by the pre-registered scan pass rule; the GT-free selector ranks structured candidates only.
A frame-sanity gate: median distance to library_v3 under 5 mm without registration. It catches whole-episode offsets such as lid ep0 [M].
Router control arm R as the default, $0 system. Spend on the agent only if R fails Stage A.
Stage A go/no-go against GT-free hand references [M]: pot sum_mm 3.035 over 8 episodes; lid 1.44 / 1.69 / 2.26; rack 5.94.
Firewall and leak-grep for scan-derived numbers (README l.29 lists scan wall thicknesses [verified]).
The beige-cup path: obs_points on the v3x ep11 track from public depth.

scores.design: Peel-and-select kit of parts: generic part library, residual peeling, depth-render selection
scores.reasons:
Strengths on automation:
- It is the most automated design: deterministic code with no object names, and no LLM in the loop.
- It costs $0 on CPU, and the core work has no permission blocker.
- It lists honestly what stays manual: the part vocabulary, priors, constants, tracks and the selector.

Strengths on integrity and reproducibility, the best of the two:
- The pre-registration includes an strace openat log covering the scans, *_align.npz and the parquets, a grep of the code, and an independent re-run that must reproduce the selection.
- Scan exposure is capped at 9-21 scorings, with no overrides.
- It declares the leakage at the selector level.
- library_v3 is always a candidate, fits that end on a bound are rejected, and t is a declared grid with pass-at-every-value. These are the right defences against silent wrong-template fits; 23 of 26 wrong-template runs exited 0 [M].
- Part A (the selector test on the frozen 48-candidate matrix) is cheap and comes early.

Risks:
1. The primary selector (z-buffered depth-render agreement) is untested, yet it carries the whole design. It is also the heaviest new build: 1.5 days.
2. 'Held-out' means odd frames of the same episode. That is not independent evidence.
3. Search step 5 accepts parts by the same S8 score that later selects. That is Goodhart pressure, with almost no hold-out to resist it.
4. Residual peeling over about 10 parts on one-sided points with 28-90 % coverage is unproven. No hand template has been reproduced by a search, and RANSAC explains only 24-60 % of points [M].
5. Removing T_MAX 6 mm is justified with the scan's 13 mm sweeper wall [D]. That is scan knowledge shaping the design, though milder than setting a value.
6. The S1 half-split QC gate cannot catch a track that is wrong but self-consistent. A track that consistently follows the other board would pass. So the [H] 'S1 rejects board 2 ep23' is probably false, and the [H] for beige ep11 is doubtful.

Cost and payoff: 7-10 agent-days for an expected [E] 0.402 -> about 0.33. Much of that the existing hand fits already deliver.
fatal_flaws: The search and the final selection use the same S8 score, held out only by odd frames of the same episode. Without independent hold-out episodes, the beam search can overfit the selector, so S8 cannot police it.

Its central bet, a GT-free selector that ranks structures across families, rests on a depth-render scorer that does not exist yet. The design does not first freeze the cheap point-based rule that already matches all 8 reference choices here [M, after the fact: fs gate plus untrimmed recall at 3 mm] as the baseline the new scorer must beat. So Part A has no real control.

Scan-informed justification: dropping T_MAX because the sweeper scan has 13 mm walls [D]. Any per-object rule or bound has to be re-derived from our own two-face evidence, or the change has to be logged as scan-informed.
best_ideas_to_graft: Pre-registration integrity package: strace -e openat with no reads under the scans directory, *_align.npz or the parquets; a grep of the method code; an independent re-run that reproduces the selection; at most 9-21 scan scorings and no overrides.
library_v3 always a candidate, plus rejection of fits that end on a parameter bound. Together these catch the silent wrong-template successes.
One marker-ball detector run first (7 mm prior, support from at least 10 frames, stem tested against a control offset), shared by every object.
All windows relative to the fitted size instead of the absolute mm constants in today's fitters.
A synthetic recovery test (points resampled from our own meshes through each episode's real coverage and noise) to calibrate lambda and the part-count recall without any ground truth.
Part A: run the selector on the frozen 48-candidate matrix by day 2-3, before the bulk of the build.

scores.design: Frozen part-program loop: an agent writes a short program in a fixed part language, an optimiser fits it to our points, and a GT-free selector picks among frozen candidates
scores.reasons:
Integrity strengths:
- It identifies the real leak paths: the scan numbers in README l.29 and the table at l.78-87, and the crop masks seeded by library_v3 (crops.py l.3-5 and 130, verified [M]).
- It answers them structurally: authoring runs through the API with no file or web access, the input bundle comes from an allowlist, and every prompt and output is grepped for leaks.
- It holds out whole episodes instead of frames.
- It has a deterministic router arm R as a control, and Stage A is a cheap ($10-20) go/no-go.
- Reproducibility comes from committing the program, the interpreter commit and the seeds.

Automation:
- The per-object choice moves to a logged agent. The vocabulary, gates, lambda and priors stay human.
- Authoring is non-deterministic, so reproducibility rests on the committed artefacts, not on re-running.

Blockers and cost:
- It needs an owner API key, which is unset [M], plus $60-110 of approved spend.
- The held-out episodes for the pitcher (ep21), sweeper (ep18) and dust pan (ep18/40) have no observed points yet [M]. Building them needs depth from the store or a GPU job, so for exactly the new objects the 'held-out' selection does not exist today.

The selector is weaker than claimed. My test [M] on 24 fresh candidates:
- The fs gate passes every under-covering plate and the sweeper board plate (+4.1 pp). It rejects a correct-family single-episode rack fit.
- Its rule (library excluded, lowest sum_mm among gate survivors) would select a board plate for the sweeper. For the pitcher it would select a board plate with a 61 mm sum, because that plate is the only survivor.
- So for every new object, the library-versus-new decision falls entirely to the scan round. The pipeline is not GT-free end to end.

Scan exposure:
- The plan scores 100-150 candidates against public scans and commits the numbers.
- Future agents and authors would then read those numbers, the same contamination route as the earlier leak.

Scan-derived prior:
- The proposed sweeper grid '{4, 8, 13}?' contains the scan's 13 mm wall, a [D] number from README l.86.
fatal_flaws: A thickness prior derived from the scans: the sweeper grid '{4, 8, 13}?' contains the 13 mm wall measured on the scan (README l.86, [D]). The project has already had to undo a scan-informed thickness prior once. As written, the protocol designer is exposed to the README, and the firewall covers only the authoring agent.

It cannot run without the owner's API key and spend approval. It also has no observed points yet for the held-out episodes of the pitcher, sweeper and dust pan, which are the objects it is meant to add.

The GT-free selector cannot finish the job [M]. Library is excluded by design. The fs gate does not penalise missing surface, so wrong-family plates pass, and sum_mm then picks them (sweeper plate at 3.274 mm, pitcher plate as the only survivor). Every new-object decision ends up resting on 100-150 public-scan scorings, which also builds a large pool of committed scan numbers that can leak into later rounds.
best_ideas_to_graft: A free-space gate from the free/hit grids that already sit in every obs file: fs_frac at most library_v3 + 5 pp, computed per episode. Paired with untrimmed recall at 3 mm and with library_v3 selectable, it matched all 8 reference first choices on the 48-candidate matrix [M, after the fact]. Freeze that pair as the baseline selector any new scorer must beat.

A structural firewall for any authoring step: no file or web tools, an input bundle built from an allowlist, and a grep of prompts and outputs for the scan numbers quoted in the docs. Extend it to whoever sets the priors and grids.
Selection on held-out episodes, not on frames of the same episode.
Arm R, a deterministic router with no agent, as a mandatory control. Any added complexity has to beat it.
Re-seed the crop masks from projected observed points before using any silhouette term, since GrabCut today is seeded by library_v3.
Stage A as a cheap go/no-go (reproduce pot, lid and rack within 5 % of the hand fits' GT-free sum_mm) before building new parts.
Flag fits with parameters on their bounds, and a flip probe that runs the kit's PCA-start ICP against our own fused points.

judges.recommendation:
The winner should be design 1's deterministic, $0, no-name pipeline with design 2's integrity and selection safeguards grafted on. Design 2's LLM authoring loop should not run now: it needs an API key and spend approval, its selector cannot do the job on its own [M], and its gain over the existing hand fits is about 0-0.045 cm [E].

Steps, in order:
1. Freeze the baseline selector in a commit now, before any build or scan contact: fs gate (fs_frac at most library_v3 + 5 pp, computed per episode), then the highest untrimmed recall at 3 mm, with library_v3 always selectable. My test [M] shows this pair matches all 8 reference first choices on the 48-candidate matrix. That is after the fact, 3 references are [E], and the sweeper margin is fs +4.1 pp. So treat it as [H] on fresh candidates.
2. Test that frozen rule on fresh candidates and new episodes. It is the control the depth-render scorer must beat in Part A; build the depth-render scorer only if the frozen rule fails.
3. Hold out whole episodes, not odd frames. First build observed points for pitcher ep21, sweeper ep18 and dust pan ep18/40 from depth already in the store. If that depth is missing, it becomes a GPU item that needs the owner's go-ahead.
4. Never let the search's acceptance score double as the final selector without that episode hold-out.
5. Delete every prior derived from the scans:
   - the 13 mm sweeper value, which design 2 puts in its grid;
   - the use of the 13 mm sweeper wall to justify dropping T_MAX, as design 1 does.
   Derive thickness from our own two-face evidence, or use a generic grid frozen before anyone looks. Extend the authoring firewall to whoever sets grids and gates, because README l.29 and l.78-87 expose scan walls, sizes and areas to every author.
6. Make loaders refuse any *_align.npz (it sits beside every obs npz), and keep design 1's strace openat audit, independent re-run and cap of 9-21 scorings. Reject design 2's 100-150 scan scorings.
7. Don't expect the S1 half-split QC gate to catch an identity swap that stays consistent across the episode (board 2 ep23). Re-tracking stays a separate item that needs the owner's go-ahead.

For the owner, in plain words: yes, today's good meshes are made per object type (a fitter per template). Once a template exists, fitting and selection already run automatically. Making the template choice automatic is about 7-10 agent-days of CPU work at $0 [E]. It mainly widens coverage; it does not close the gap to the leaders (0.11-0.15 cm against our 0.402 cm).

synth.honest_answer: Partly, yes. An agent wrote each good mesh's part list after looking at that object: pot = bowl-shaped lathe + flat bar handle + marker balls, lid = dome + strap, rack = tray + cup holder + pegs, boards = slab. About a third of the fitter code (461 of 1,397 lines in prim_potlid.py and prim_boards.py [M]) only makes sense for one object, for example "the handle is the cluster that reaches more than 60 mm beyond the body" or "the lid flange lies at 40-80 mm". The rest is already generic: about 38 % runs on any object (loading, marker balls, clustering, watertight union, outline extrusion, the multi-episode driver) and about 19 % covers a whole shape family (open-container lathe, flat slab). Once a template exists, everything after it is automatic: every size is fitted to our own stereo points, variants are generated, and a score that never sees a scan picks the winner. Choosing the template is not automatic. Run a fitter on the wrong object and it quietly returns a clean but wrong mesh (23 of 26 such test runs did [M]); only the selector catches it. There is an automated route, built from these generic parts and a ground-truth-free check that library_v3 must be beaten on. On the 48 meshes we already have, that check picks the right one for all 8 objects [M], but this was found after the fact, so two cheap probes must confirm it before the build. Expect it mostly to widen coverage (dust pan, sweeper, cup handles) and save hand work, reaching about 0.33 cm [E], not to close the gap to the leaders (0.11-0.15 cm). synth.recommended_design:
Name-blind router with peel-and-select parts and a frozen two-sided GT-free gate. It is a hybrid: design 1's deterministic, $0, CPU pipeline with no object names in the code, plus design 2's safeguards and its no-agent router arm as the default. Design 2's LLM authoring loop becomes an optional arm, used only where the router fails and only after the owner approves an API key and spend.

How it works:
1. Each episode's points pass integrity and frame gates.
2. Marker balls are found first by one shared detector.
3. Several body hypotheses are fitted from a fixed generic part library. Every window is relative to the fitted size.
4. The residual is peeled cluster by cluster. Each cluster tries {leave out, ball, extruded plate in its own plane, swept tube, TSDF patch}. A part is accepted only if it raises untrimmed recall without putting surface where our cameras saw empty space. The trimmed obs_fidelity is not used here because it hides parts under 10 % of the points, and the pot handle is about 7 %.
5. Unseen thicknesses are declared priors on a generic grid {1.5, 2.5, 4.0} mm. Each must pass at every value and is never chosen by fidelity.
6. A frozen selector applies these gates:
   - fs_frac <= library_v3 + 5 pp;
   - untrimmed rec3 >= library_v3 - 0.05 on a held-out episode, or odd frames when only one episode exists;
   - <= 20 % of parameters on a bound;
   - watertight, <= 4096 faces after budget_mesh;
   - frame sanity: median distance to library_v3 < 5 mm without registration;
   - 0 flips in pipeline/mesh_gates.py flip_check at the eval seeds.
   Survivors are ranked by obs_fidelity sum_mm + lambda*k. If nothing survives, library_v3 is kept.
7. Whether library or new wins, and whether hand kit or new wins, is decided only by the pre-registered scan pass rule: CD-O <= baseline - 0.03 cm, ADD <= baseline + 1 mm, 0 flips. That round allows 9-21 scorings and no overrides.

Evidence for the gate [M, this synthesis, script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/90d4009c-b597-536b-9d55-58f81afca135/scratchpad/synth/join.py over the existing matrix_scores.jsonl, fs_matrix.jsonl and the fs_frac outputs of autoloop_probe, judge1_fs and judge2]. The rule picks the reference on 8 of 8 objects: cup lathe, pot ep41 fit, lid t2.5 fit, rack joint_v2, board 1 occ_d2, and library for the sweeper, pitcher and dust pan.
- Sweeper: the board plate passes fs (11.48 vs 7.39 %) but fails the recall floor (0.749 < 0.782).
- Dust pan: the lid template's phantom strap passes recall (0.716) but fails fs (41.1 vs 0.75 %).
- Rack: joint_v2 survives (fs 6.1 %, rec3 0.647) even though library_v3 has the lower sum_mm (8.57 vs 9.32).

Caveats: this result is post hoc; 3 of the 8 references are [E]; and on board 1 it picks occ_d2, which flips 1/6 [D]. So the flip gate is required, and whether that GT-free gate catches this flip is [H].

The design does not replace the hand kits now. They are the incumbents for pot, lid and rack. The automated route must first rediscover their structure blind (probe P1) and cover a new object (probe P2).

Integrity: this synthesis read only non-align obs npz keys, our own score JSONL files, our own fit JSON and repo docs. No scan, *_align.npz, mocap or parquet pose was opened, and no repo file was edited.
architecture: A0 Integrity layer. One allowlisted loader reads only the obs npz keys pts, cam, frame, hits, free, lo and vox. It refuses *_align.npz (one sits beside every obs file), the scan directory and the parquets. Object names are file keys only, with no branch on them, and a grep of the method code is committed. Anyone who sets priors or grids works from a frozen generic list, because README l.29 and l.86 quote scan wall thicknesses (for example the sweeper's 13 mm). Rounds carry an strace openat log and an independent re-run.

A1 Inputs (GT-free): obs_points.py points on our own tracks; library_v3 as fallback candidate, TSDF-patch source and frame reference; our tracked poses and calib; colour crops, with masks re-seeded from projected obs points (crops.py GrabCut is seeded by library_v3 and would favour it).

A2 Episode gates. Frame sanity: median obs-to-library_v3 distance < 5 mm with no registration; it catches lid ep0, which is 23-26 mm off [M judge]. Half-split self-consistency catches unstable tracks but cannot catch a consistent identity swap such as board 2 ep23. Failing episodes go to a re-track list.

A3 Preprocess: 1.5 mm voxels, camera-oriented normals, up taken from the table plane and the camera side, object scale s = robust RMS radius. Every window is a fraction of s or of the fitted part. This replaces the absolute 60 mm handle reach, the 40-80 mm flange, the 15-35 mm dome, the 50 mm arch, NFACE 1500 and T_MAX 6 mm.

A4 One marker detector, run first. It merges prim_potlid set A and prim_boards set B: centre votes with R0 = 7 mm (from our own spoon stereo), >= 10 frames of support, a stem only where points beat a 20 mm control offset, and rejection of any centre inside a fitted solid. It fixes the false ball on the dust-pan patch [M].

A5 Body proposals: lathe (pot_axis and lathe_obs.fit_axis, both orientations); sheet of revolution (the lid's edge-circle and tilt LSQ); plate set (region growing on normals with RANSAC seeds); slab (prim_boards fit_plane plus occupancy outline); drafted rounded-rect shell (prim_rack rrect_sd and cup_lsq without the hard-coded face signs); TSDF only (library_v3). Slippage and RANSAC hints only order the search.

A6 Generic part library. Each part has a fit-from-points routine, a parameter count k, relative bounds and a bound-hit flag: P1 thin-wall lathe; P2 sheet of revolution; P3 extruded outline in the part's own plane, also used as the generic handle plate, so seen holes come from occupancy; P4 folded plate set (new); P5 drafted shell or tube; P6 swept tube or strap (the arch_strap sweep plus a new centreline fit); P7 peg or cone with a shared template per row; P8 rounded box; P9 marker ball on a stem; P10 TSDF patch (tsdf_parts).

A7 Residual peeling. Residual = points more than max(4 mm, 2 sigma) outside the body, clustered with 3 mm voxels (prim_potlid.clusters). Each cluster tries {leave out, P9, P3, P6, P7, P10}. A part is accepted on an untrimmed rec3 gain >= 0.01 with an fs_frac rise <= 1 pp, never on trimmed sum_mm. Beam width 4, at most 8 parts. A fit ending on a bound is rejected. Parts are joined with a manifold3d union, then budget_mesh is applied.

A8 Declared priors for geometry we never see. Unseen undersides and floors use the grid {1.5, 2.5, 4.0} mm, fixed before any look and containing no scan values. Base = table-contact plate; containers get a closed floor. Thickness is measured only when two-wall or two-face evidence exists (>= 3 bins, or a relative point count). Pass at every grid value; submit the middle one.

A9 Frozen GT-free selector, committed before any new candidate exists. Gates: fs_frac <= library_v3 + 5 pp; rec3 >= library_v3 - 0.05 on a held-out episode, or odd frames; bound hits <= 20 %; watertight; <= 4096 faces; frame sanity; 0 flips in mesh_gates flip_check. Survivors are ranked by held-out sum_mm + lambda*k, with lambda calibrated on synthetic recoveries. If nothing survives, library_v3 stays.

A10 Decision layer. A structured candidate replaces library_v3, or a hand kit, only by the pre-registered scan pass rule. Each round commits a manifest, makes 9-21 scorings and allows no overrides. Nothing is ever tuned on eval.
A11 Output in the library frame. Eval meshes are rebuilt from public episodes with the same SHA, so no eval depth is needed. The exception is the spoon, which needs eval points.

A12 Optional agent arm (design 2), only for objects where A5-A9 fail. A Claude API tool loop with no file or web access writes a short program in the A6 part language. Requires the owner's API key and spend approval; prompts and outputs are leak-grepped.
grafted_from_runners_up: From design 2: the free-space gate fs_frac, computed from the 4 mm free/hit grids that every obs file already stores. It measures precision. [M] 11 of 11 wrong templates were rejected.

From design 2: the GT-free selector only ranks structured candidates. Library versus new, and hand kit versus new, is decided by the pre-registered scan pass rule, because sum_mm alone prefers library over the [D]-better rack fit (5.53 vs 5.94 mm over 5 episodes).
From design 2: hold out whole episodes, not frames of the same episode, wherever an object has 2 or more episodes. Odd-frame hold-out is only the fallback, and it is declared as such.
From design 2: the deterministic router arm R becomes the default system. The LLM authoring arm is an optional add-on that must beat R in a cheap Stage A ($10-20 [design 2 estimate]).
From design 2: firewall and leak-grep for any authoring step, extended (judge 2) to whoever sets grids and gates.
From design 2: re-seed the crop masks from projected obs points before any silhouette term.
From design 2: the beige-cup path, running obs_points along the existing v3x ep11 track from public depth.

From design 1: an untrimmed rec3 completeness floor, paired with fs_frac. Each fails alone [M]: fs alone passes the sweeper board plate and the pitcher plate fragment; recall alone passes the dust-pan phantom strap.
From design 1: reject any fit that ends on a parameter bound. The rack fitter on the pitcher and sweeper, and the lid strap on the dust pan, were silent bound-hit failures [M].

From design 1: unseen thickness comes from a grid that must pass at every value and is never chosen by fidelity. [M] Standard fidelity prefers the thinnest lid: 1.436 / 1.686 / 2.259 mm at t = 1.5 / 2.5 / 4.0.

From design 1: one marker detector shared by every object, all windows relative to the fitted size, residual peeling with a beam, manifold3d union with budget_mesh, and a synthetic recovery test (our own meshes resampled through real coverage and noise) to calibrate lambda.
From design 1: a pre-registration integrity package (strace openat, code grep, independent re-run), a cap of 9-21 scan scorings, no overrides, and the hard 0-flip gate via pipeline/mesh_gates.py.
From judge 1: a frame-sanity gate, median distance to library_v3 < 5 mm without registration. [M] Lid ep0 sits 23-26 mm off while ep2 sits at 1.4-1.7 mm.

From judges 1 and 2: freeze the combined selector first and use it as the control that any depth-render scorer must beat. Build the depth-render scorer only if the frozen rule fails on fresh candidates.

From judge 2: remove every scan-derived number from priors and justifications. That includes the 13 mm sweeper grid value and using the 13 mm scan wall to argue for dropping T_MAX. T_MAX goes because the windows become relative, not because of the scan.
From judge 2: loaders refuse *_align.npz; reject design 2's 100-150 scan scorings; do not expect the half-split QC to catch identity swaps.
From judge 1: swap the meshes that already pass first (pot, lid, rack; blue-cup lathe ep21), before any new method. Prioritise the remaining work by pairs.

synth.what_stays_manual:
These still need a person:

1. The part vocabulary. 'No object names in code' does not mean 'no object knowledge': about 10 part types chosen by people who have seen these objects. A new kind of geometry (bristles, hinges, cloth, a pouring spout) needs a new part written by a person or an agent.
2. Priors for geometry we never see: the thickness grid, the table-contact base, closed floors. Our points cannot settle them ([M] the lid t-grid), so they stay declared and frozen human choices under the pass-at-every-value rule, set by someone who has not read the scan thickness numbers in README l.29/86.
3. Global constants and the selector itself: stereo noise scale, residual distance, the 7 mm marker radius, the gate margins (+5 pp, -0.05), beam width and the protocol for calibrating lambda. The selector was designed once after seeing which scores match existing [D] orders (selector-level leakage, declared) and must stay frozen.
4. Upstream tracks: beige cup ep11, board 2 ep23, lid ep0. No mesher fixes a wrong track; re-tracking and eval depth for the spoon are GPU jobs that need the owner's go-ahead.
5. Writing each pre-registration, reading the scan round, visual QA, and diagnosing a failed object (add a part type or keep the incumbent).
6. The owner's submission decisions: pack-only versus a simulator-copy re-run, and any rental or API spend.
expected_gains: Stage 0, no new method: swapping the pot, lid and rack meshes that already pass takes CD-O from 0.402 to about 0.367 cm. Adding the blue-cup lathe ep21 (0.523 -> 0.291 [D]) brings it to about 0.335 cm [E, assumes eval pairs match the public scans]. ADD also falls on all four (pot 6.7 -> 3.05 mm, lid 8.1 -> 4.46, rack 6.0 -> 5.37, cup 10.0 -> 4.1 [D]); the AUC effect is unmeasured.

The automated route's own CD-O gain on top of Stage 0 is small. If the dust pan reaches Design O's 0.251 and the sweeper the single-episode TSDF's 0.271 [D], that is about -0.007 cm overall [E]. A cup-handle increment is unquantified [H]. Overall about 0.31-0.33 cm [E].
Beige cup, if re-tracked or rebuilt on v3x ep11 and reaching 0.25-0.35 [E]: about -0.025 cm overall, the largest single non-spoon lever.
Spoon (10 of 36 pairs): unknown. It is about 0.18 cm inferred and cannot be checked against a scan; any gain needs eval depth and the owner's go-ahead.

Hand work: a new object goes from about 300-450 lines of object-specific fitter code plus an agent's template choice to 0 new code, as long as its shape fits the part vocabulary. Wrong-template runs stop being silent: they are rejected by the gates and library_v3 is kept ([M] 11 of 11 rejected by fs, and 8 of 8 correct references under the combined rule).
Not expected: closing the gap to the leaders (0.112-0.154 cm). That needs better tracks, the spoon, and probably thinner-than-observed priors validated in rounds, not just automation.
